top_papers.title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a "metacognitive controller" to guide diffusion language models for agent tasks. This controller learns to decide when to stop generating tokens and how much text to produce, optimizing computation based on the agent's interaction needs. The core contribution is an efficient inference method that reduces computational cost by intelligently managing generation length, leading to significant FLOPs reduction while maintaining task accuracy.

top_papers.title: Agent-Conditioned Routing: Diverse Reasoning Paths Within One Frozen Model
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Agent-Conditioned Routing (ACR), a method to elicit diverse reasoning paths from a single frozen Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model. ACR achieves this by assigning persistent, untrained expert-eligibility masks to parallel trajectories, allowing them to explore different reasoning strategies without fine-tuning or model copies. The contribution lies in demonstrating ACR's ability to generate significantly more distinct solution methods compared to standard sampling techniques on a challenging benchmark.
top_papers.figure_caption: Architecture of ACR . Four copies of an identical prompt share one frozen MoE backbone. Persistent shared/private masks give trajectories distinct expert eligibility while preserving the learned token router.

top_papers.title: Concordat: Typed Sessions for LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: Concordat enforces LLM agent actions by treating their interfaces as finite-state protocols, similar to typestate and session types. This ensures that agents only use allowed tools at each step, preventing unauthorized actions and enforcing human-defined rules at runtime. The core contribution is a system that provides robust, verifiable control over LLM agent behavior, enhancing safety and reliability for consequential tasks.

top_papers.title: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces SimpleLoRIF, a gradient embedding method to detect safety-degrading training data for LLMs. It works by identifying fine-tuning examples whose gradients correlate with unsafe behavior, even when the examples themselves appear benign. This scalable approach allows for practical filtering of large datasets, enabling the creation of safer LLMs.
top_papers.figure_caption: Detection AUC against embedding wall-clock time for each optimization strategy. Restricting backpropagation to the last four transformer blocks gives the best balance of embedding quality and speed.

top_papers.title: Gym-Anything-RT: Scaling Real-Time Environments for Vision-Language Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Gym-Anything-RT, a framework for evaluating vision-language agents in real-time interactive environments. Its core method involves automatically generating visual minigames that test an agent's ability to perceive and act within a dynamically changing environment. The contribution is a novel benchmark for understanding and scaling the real-time interaction capabilities of these agents, which are crucial for applications like video games and robotics.
top_papers.figure_caption: Examples of real-time minigames generated with Gym-Anything-RT . The 100 minigames in our benchmark cover different combinations of capabilities, with controlled variations in difficulty and interaction.

top_papers.title: PerceptRL: Making Visual Perception Rewardable in MLLMs from Answers to Interactions
top_papers.abstract: PerceptRL addresses the challenge of improving visual perception in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) during post-training. Its core method uses a multi-agent reinforcement learning pipeline to extract verifiable perceptual errors from image captions and convert them into question-answering tasks with automated rewards. This approach strengthens perception by generating targeted, rewardable feedback, ultimately improving MLLM performance.

top_papers.title: Uncovering Why LLMs Fail: From Internal Mechanisms to Adversarial Reasoning Trajectories
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces CauTrace, a white-box diagnostic framework to understand LLM failures. It analyzes internal mechanisms like functional states, representation propagation, and temporal coordination to reveal how reasoning errors develop, both in ordinary and adversarial scenarios. The core contribution is a method to trace failure trajectories, offering insights beyond just final output correctness.
top_papers.figure_caption: CauTrace overview. CauTrace maps clean/adversarial traces to seven functional-state coordinates and analyzes (1) Propagation of Representation across Transformer blocks; (2) Temporal-state Coordination among support, commitment, and verification; and (3) Reasoning Trajectory over the full generation trace.

top_papers.title: When Visual Evidence Is Insufficient: How Instructions, Post-Training, and Internal Activations Shape Refusal in Multimodal Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how multimodal language models (MLLMs) learn to refuse answering questions when visual evidence is insufficient. The core method involves systematically manipulating instructions, post-training techniques, and internal model activations across different MLLMs. The key contribution is demonstrating that refusal is highly sensitive to the precise wording and placement of instructions, and that these effects are often model-specific and can be masked by aggregate analysis.
top_papers.figure_caption: Distinguishing three model behaviors to visually unanswerable questions: solvability detection, selective, and evidence-based. In this work, we study evidence-based refusal and the factors that shape this behavior.

top_papers.title: ETAMem: Decoupling and Aligning Heterogeneous Memory for Long-Term Conversational Agents
top_papers.abstract: ETAMem addresses challenges in long-term conversational memory by decoupling heterogeneous information and aligning memory organization with its characteristics. It parses information into atomic units, identifies affective content, and structures memory into three complementary hierarchical views: Event, Affect, and Time. This multi-view approach enables more coherent and personalized interactions for LLMs.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Illustration of challenges in existing memory systems and our proposed multi-view memory framework.

top_papers.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
top_papers.abstract: GEPA-Curator addresses limitations in self-improving agents by introducing a curation mechanism for learning experiences. It filters out potentially harmful or noisy failures and prioritizes learning from successful past interactions, thereby improving the agent's ability to optimize its prompts and perform better in complex tasks.
top_papers.figure_caption: GEPA-Curator system diagram. The prompt optimizer takes in a minibatch of tasks at each iteration and invokes the actor agent to execute them and performs reflective prompt optimization based on the resulting trajectories. The Curator augments the prompt optimizer by acting as an outer-loop process which traverses through the training dataset and constructs each minibatch to pass into the prompt optimizer. The Curator reads past execution trajectories for each task sampled from the training dataset and decides to run the task if doing so is likely to provide useful optimization signal (Section 3.1 ). The Curator can also pass prior successful trajectories for failed tasks as context to the prompt optimizer as a trusted reference example (Section 3.2 ). Once the curated training batch of selected tasks and successful context is constructed, it is passed to the prompt optimizer for execution and optimization. The resulting trajectories and evaluation outcomes are then written back to the task history for use in subsequent curation rounds.

top_papers.title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a "metacognitive controller" that efficiently guides diffusion language models for agent tasks. The controller learns to decide when to finalize tokens and how much text to generate, optimizing computation based on the agent's interaction needs. This approach significantly reduces inference costs while maintaining task accuracy.

top_papers.title: Agentic University: Collaborative Agents for Personalized Learning
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Agentic University (AU), a novel system that uses a multi-agent organization to facilitate personalized learning. AU's core method involves learners collaborating with specialized agents to create and maintain a dynamic "Capability Program." This program aligns personal goals, activities, and assessments, with learner feedback and performance guiding the learning process. The key contribution is demonstrating AU's effectiveness in improving program organization, assessment design, and revision quality, leading to significantly higher assessment gains and enhanced cognitive support for learners.
top_papers.figure_caption: Two ways of organizing multi-agent work around a learner. Left: a learner provides a request, and agents collaborate to generate learning artifacts. Right: a learner participates as a member of a multi-agent organization. Its activities support learning, while learner feedback and performance inform subsequent work.

top_papers.title: How I Aligned Your Model: Scaling Up Multilingual Safety Training with Templates
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses the English-centric bias in LLM safety training by proposing a scalable template-based method to generate massive multilingual safety datasets. The core contribution is the MSafeTemp corpus, which uses translated and culturally localized templates to create both harmful and benign prompts across 60 languages, enabling more comprehensive multilingual safety alignment and evaluation. This work demonstrates that English-only evaluations are insufficient and can mask significant multilingual safety vulnerabilities.
top_papers.figure_caption: The MSafeTemp pipeline. Original prompt goes through extraction of harmful terms, validation, translation, and a targeted judge pass of a template. Three branches then produce generic harmful variants ( TR ), exact-fill benign controls ( OR ), and culturally localized variants ( PH ). English ( EN ) follows the same path without translation.

top_papers.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes "unified training," a single algorithm capable of performing all stages of foundation model training (pretraining, midtraining, SFT, RL). It achieves this by framing RL objectives as maximum-likelihood fitting to model-generated data. The core contribution is demonstrating that staged training is not fundamentally necessary, leading to improved accuracy-compute tradeoffs, broader task coverage, and better continual learning capabilities.

top_papers.title: A Low-Rank Space Captures Linear Alignment Between LLM and Human Neural Activity During Naturalistic Language Listening
top_papers.abstract: This paper uses a low-rank regression method to find the most important parts of Large Language Model (LLM) representations for predicting human brain activity during language listening. They discovered that only a tiny fraction (1-3%) of the LLM's representational space is needed to accurately predict neural responses, suggesting that brain-predictive information is highly concentrated and partially shared across models and individuals.
top_papers.figure_caption: (a) We view alignment as a measure of the linear features shared by the LLM embedding space and the neural response space. Our goal is to selectively extract the intersection of the two spaces. (b) Our pipeline. We learn two low-rank representations of the model embeddings and use them to predict neural data. The PCA space (green) prioritizes capturing the directions of principal variation in the LLM embeddings. The RRR space (blue) prioritizes the directions which best align between the two representational spaces teasing out the aligned subspace. (c) To identify the size of the aligned subspace we sweep the subspace rank, fit new models and re-evaluate. We find the point at which our RRR space performance saturates and compare it to the PCA point of saturation. (d) Leave-one-subject-out experiment. We fit the RRR space on all but one subject and then transfer the projection matrix to a held-out subject and fit a new mapping to that subject’s neural data. (e) We again sweep over ranks and compare the point of saturation on the held-out subject between the RRR space fit on all subjects, RRR space fit on all but the held-out subject, and the unsupervised PCA space.

top_papers.title: Agentic LLM reasoning in pediatric diabetes outcome prediction from multimodal medical records
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces CEDAR, an LLM agent pipeline for predicting pediatric diabetes outcomes from multimodal medical records. CEDAR demonstrates superior prediction accuracy compared to traditional machine learning models, even for rare outcomes, by leveraging evidence-citing and self-auditing capabilities. Its strong performance and high agreement with expert clinicians highlight its potential for improving clinical decision-making in pediatric diabetes.

top_papers.title: Don't Lose the Thread: Empowering Long-Horizon LLM Agents with Cognitive Resource Self-Allocation
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces CORAL, a method for LLM agents to manage their working memory on long-horizon tasks. CORAL allows agents to proactively checkpoint progress and verified facts, then reset cluttered context to resume reasoning from a clean state, preventing cognitive overload. This self-allocation of cognitive resources significantly improves LLM agent performance on complex, extended reasoning challenges.

top_papers.title: Admission Without Answers: Label-Free Certification and Experience Learning for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces ADMITOR, a novel label-free method for admitting reliable optimization models generated by LLMs. ADMITOR achieves this by generating multiple models, testing them on resampled problem instances, and admitting those with consistent optimal values across different model families. Its key contribution is enabling robust experience learning for LLM-based optimization without requiring ground-truth answers, significantly improving the precision of admitted candidate models.

top_papers.title: Affective Flow Language Model for Emotional Support Conversation
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the Affective Flow Language Model (AFlow) to improve emotional support conversations. AFlow models the dialogue as an "affective utility flow," allowing it to estimate the value of intermediate conversation states and potential strategies. Its contribution lies in the Affective Flow Preference Optimization (AFPO) method, which uses this flow concept to propagate feedback from overall dialogue success to guide the model's sequential strategy decisions in multi-turn interactions.
top_papers.figure_caption: Comparison of emotional support conversation approaches.

top_papers.title: Efficient Reasoning Training Does Not Always Harm CoT Faithfulness and Monitorability
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether efficient Chain-of-Thought (CoT) training harms faithfulness and monitorability in large language models. The authors fine-tune models using three distinct length-pressure methods and evaluate their impact on how well the CoT reflects the model's decision-making process. Their contribution lies in demonstrating that efficient reasoning training does not *always* negatively affect CoT faithfulness, depending on the specific efficiency method and task.
top_papers.figure_caption: Efficient reasoning training reduces CoT faithfulness but largely preserves monitorability. (1) We train models with three methods that reward CoT length differently. (2) Then we measure whether the CoT predicts the model’s answers on related inputs (faithfulness) and whether it reveals when an intervention influenced the answer (monitorability). (3) In this example, a ∼ \( \sim \) 70% shorter CoT loses faithfulness due to output inconsistency, while monitorability is unchanged.

top_papers.title: FrugalEvo: Towards Cost-Aware LLM-Guided Program Evolution
top_papers.abstract: FrugalEvo introduces a cost-aware evolutionary framework for LLM-guided program optimization. It leverages a two-tiered LLM approach, with a powerful LLM guiding strategy and a cheaper LLM implementing and refining code, to maximize performance gain per unit cost. The contribution lies in this cost-efficient design and a new metric, BA-AUC, for evaluating performance within a fixed budget.

top_papers.title: HazardWeaver: Scientific Route Selection for Hazard Analysis Agents
top_papers.abstract: HazardWeaver addresses the challenge of AI agents selecting appropriate scientific methods for hazard analysis by formulating it as state-dependent route selection. Its core method involves compiling evidence-linked conditions for scientific applicability and representing executable capabilities in a graph to check compatibility. This enables agents to dynamically choose and adapt scientific workflows based on evolving evidence and available tools.
top_papers.figure_caption: Global coverage of HWB.

top_papers.title: HyperBrowseComp: A Multilingual and Multimodal Stress Test for Web-Browsing Agents
top_papers.abstract: HyperBrowseComp is a new benchmark designed to rigorously test web-browsing agents. Its core method involves creating extremely challenging, multilingual, and multimodal questions that require agents to locate obscure information, follow complex clue chains, and synthesize data from diverse sources like videos and scanned documents. The contribution is a robust evaluation tool that pushes the boundaries of agent capabilities in persistent information seeking, going beyond simple parametric knowledge.
top_papers.figure_caption: Example question and evidence route from HyperBrowseComp . Solving it requires locating a specific moment in a video, grounding the scene to a real-world location, and retrieving information from a financial report.

top_papers.title: MobiAgent: Dual-Loop Recursive Policy Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation
top_papers.abstract: MobiAgent tackles long-horizon mobile manipulation by introducing a dual-loop framework for robust deployment and continuous self-improvement. The Inner Loop uses a Vision-Language Model to dynamically compose atomic skills for receding-horizon planning and error recovery. The Outer Loop recursively refines these skills through self-generated trajectories, enabling continuous learning and adaptation beyond initial training.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of MobiAgent. MobiAgent solves a long-horizon picking_up_trash task by interleaving dynamic planning, skill-conditioned execution, and critic-guided recovery. The rollout trace illustrates a failed placement where the can drops outside the trash. In response, MobiAgent triggers replanning, guiding the robot to approach the displaced can, re-grasp it, and complete the task. This behavior is driven by our dual-loop framework (bottom left), which couples an online Inner Loop executing atomic skills with an offline Outer Loop that autonomously curates data for continuous policy evolution. The bottom right shows real-robot deployment on paper, bottle, and can disposal, as well as pouring blue particles into a cup.

top_papers.title: NeutronGym: Physics-Graded Neutron Instrument Design for LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: NeutronGym is a novel, executable environment designed to test whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can truly perform physics-based design rather than just recall information. It allows LLM agents to build neutron instruments by validating tools, with McStas ray-tracing and a physics-graded ladder evaluating their creations. The paper's core contribution is this physics-graded environment, which demonstrates current LLMs struggle with complex scientific instrument design, even after training.

top_papers.title: IDRF: Inverse-Distilled Reward Fine-tuning of Masked Discrete Diffusion Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces IDRF, a framework for efficiently fine-tuning masked discrete diffusion models with rewards. IDRF replaces computationally expensive sequence-level KL divergence with an "inverse-distillation regularization" that is provably equivalent under optimal conditions. This allows for reward optimization using the model's own few-step sampler, achieving strong performance across various generation tasks without needing a separate reference model.
top_papers.figure_caption: IDRF (ours) across DNA, images, and text. Reward-only fine-tuning and IDRF sample with the same budget of 8 8 , 4 4 , and 32 32 steps. Reward-only fine-tuning hacks the reward: DNA lacks accessibility (ATAC-Acc), images blur, and reviews degenerate into repetition that rarely ends with EOS. IDRF avoids these failures.

top_papers.title: UniIntervene++: An Adaptive Intervention Agent for Efficient Real-World Reinforcement Learning
top_papers.abstract: UniIntervene++ introduces an adaptive intervention agent for online reinforcement learning in robots. It learns to dynamically switch between autonomous execution and various assisted behaviors by formulating them as "Options" within a unified semi-Markov decision process. This approach ensures interventions remain relevant as the robot's competence evolves, leading to more efficient real-world learning.

top_papers.title: CLIMB: Confidence-Guided Complementary Evidence for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
top_papers.abstract: CLIMB is a training-free framework for multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) that improves knowledge-intensive visual question answering. It first creates a diverse pool of relevant textual evidence using a redundancy-reducing objective. Then, it refines the answer by selecting evidence based on relevance, specificity, and cross-modal alignment, only accepting an updated answer if it demonstrably increases confidence.
top_papers.figure_caption: Comparison of multimodal RAG approaches. (a) Standard methods Cocchi et al. (2025) ; Caffagni et al. (2024b) ; Yan and Xie (2024) rely on Top-K similarity selection, which often produces redundant evidence with limited coverage and lacks explicit quality control for answer generation. (b) Our CLIMB framework addresses these limitations through two key innovations: diversity-aware evidence construction that balances relevance and complementarity to build a non-redundant passage pool, and confidence-controlled decoding that uses multi-faceted scoring and monotonic confidence constraints to ensure reliable answer updates.

top_papers.title: Passing the Test You Trained On: Re-evaluating Prompt-Injection Detectors for LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper re-evaluates prompt-injection detectors used by LLM agents, finding that their performance on public benchmarks doesn't reliably predict their effectiveness within actual agents. By replaying tool calls from agent benchmarks, the authors demonstrate significant performance discrepancies and poor transferability of detection rankings across different benchmarks. Their contribution highlights the inadequacy of current evaluation methods and suggests that the training data's characteristics heavily influence detector performance.

top_papers.title: BazaarBench: Delegation Safety in Decentralized C2C Marketplaces Run by LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces BazaarBench, a simulated decentralized C2C marketplace designed to evaluate the safety of LLM agents acting on behalf of users. BazaarBench tracks transaction integrity and uses a combination of record checks and LLM judgments to identify six types of failures across five stages of the marketplace process. The contribution lies in providing a novel benchmark for assessing and improving the trustworthiness and security of LLM agents in real-world decentralized trading environments.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of BazaarBench. The left panel illustrates a marketplace interaction, including optional inspection. The right panels show market construction, an agent’s actions within one two-hour tick, the checks and LLM judge used for evaluation, the six failure types, and the base markets and their L1–L3 continuations.

top_papers.title: Can Agent Harnesses and Inference Engines Hear Each Other? The HEAR Protocol for Agentic LLM Serving
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the HEAR protocol, a bidirectional communication standard for agentic LLM serving. HEAR enables agent harnesses and inference engines to share crucial information, such as workflow intent and runtime state, respectively. This standardized interface facilitates workflow-aware execution by allowing for diverse coordination strategies without altering core semantics.
top_papers.figure_caption: Motivating example. Without workflow intent, the engine may evict KV state shortly before reuse; without KV-residency feedback, the harness may schedule a cold request before an equivalent cache-resident one.

top_papers.title: CLIFT: Conformal Self-Verification for Web Agent Training and Test-Time Scaling
top_papers.abstract: CLIFT addresses the challenge of training web agents by using a self-verification mechanism. During training, the agent generates verification questions about its actions, and a "Compositional Conformal Certifier" uses these questions to provide more informative, signed rewards. At test time, this certified evidence is reused to select the best trajectories, improving agent performance without relying on expensive external judges.

top_papers.title: Closing the Context Gap: Activation Alignment for Tabular In-Context Learning
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces **Activation Alignment**, a novel method to improve in-context learning (ICL) for tabular foundation models. It addresses the trade-off between prediction cost and performance by training a lightweight linear transformation to align the intermediate activations of a model using partial context with a model using full context. This approach allows for efficient ICL without sacrificing accuracy, as demonstrated on a large benchmark.

top_papers.title: HERA: Harness-Environment Co-Evolution for Reliable Agentic Abstention
top_papers.abstract: HERA addresses the challenge of LLM agents failing to abstain from impossible tasks by introducing a co-evolutionary framework. It automatically generates feasible and infeasible task pairs by mutating environments and uses performance failures to adapt the agent's harness and create new, targeted tasks. This approach significantly improves generalization to unseen failure modes.
top_papers.figure_caption: Harness–environment co-evolution. Given an environment pool of feasible and infeasible tasks and current harness, paired rollouts and failure diagnosis are used to iteratively evolve both the environment pool and harness. Environment evolution (top) constructs, validates, and selects new feasible–infeasible task pairs to challenge the current agent and expand the training pool. Harness evolution (bottom) similarly refines the harness iteratively on the expanded task pool, with each updated harness selected from candidates using performance on a validation set.

top_papers.title: Learning to Read the Contextual Tokens in Diffusion Transformers
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a method to interrogate the internal "contextual tokens" of Diffusion Transformers used for multimodal generation. By training a lightweight network to map these tokens to a frozen LLM, the authors demonstrate that these tokens encode rich, evolving scene semantics. This allows for natural language questioning of the image generation process, revealing that early stages capture global attributes and later stages refine finer details.

top_papers.title: Recursive Video In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Recursive Video In-Context Learning (RV-ICL), a method that transforms demonstration videos into a hierarchical structure for LLM agents. Instead of a flat prompt, the agent navigates this hierarchy, starting with coarse task structure and drilling down to finer details like specific moments or clips as needed during execution. This allows agents to learn from demonstrations more effectively by providing contextually relevant visual information without slowing down the entire process.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of RV-ICL on a task from the LIBERO-10 suite of LIBERO-PRO. The agent receives one demonstration of the task as a hierarchy (a) and consults it while solving the same task in a new layout (b). (a) The hierarchy has four levels: L 0 L_{0} event-driven keyframes (thin lines mark their time), L 1 L_{1} phases between grasps and releases, L 2 L_{2} moments around each sub-event, and L 3 L_{3} 20-frame clips, here of the first grasp. (b) The tool calls of one solved evaluation episode (consecutive calls grouped, robot actions in grey, re-entries in orange). The agent reads L 0 L_{0} – L 2 L_{2} while planning and loads clips only during execution. Each re-entry loads the clip of the current sub-goal: the grasp, the release or the closing of the door.

top_papers.title: The Pushback Paradox: A Two-Probe Diagnostic for Language Model Compliance
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel two-probe benchmark to measure language model compliance. The "active probe" assesses exploitability by observing if a model accepts a lower payoff when instructed, while the "passive probe" measures stoppability by checking if it relinquishes a higher payoff when told to wait. This benchmark provides a "compliance index" ($κ$) to categorize models, revealing that most current models are compliant in both aspects, but few can be stopped without being exploitable.

top_papers.title: Aligning Multimodal Patient Evidence with Biomedical Knowledge Graphs for Clinical LLMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces MM-KG, a novel method for explicitly linking multimodal patient data (like text, images, and genomics) with biomedical knowledge graphs. By representing these as a unified, typed graph with alignment edges, MM-KG allows for traceable and adjustable connections. This enables clinical LLMs to better leverage and understand the evidence behind their reasoning.
top_papers.figure_caption: Motivation of MM-KG.

top_papers.title: What Matters for Latent Reasoning with Flow Matching
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Flow-based Latent Reasoning (FLaRe), a method for LLMs to reason in a continuous latent space before verbalizing the answer. FLaRe's core method uses flow matching to train this latent space, ensuring reasoning is useful, diverse, explainable, refinable, and efficient. Its main contribution is a recipe for effectively training such latent spaces, addressing limitations of prior approaches that often learn shortcuts or imitate explicit reasoning.

top_papers.title: Improving Diversity in LLM Short Story Generation
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces DivLM, a post-training framework to improve diversity in LLM-generated short stories. DivLM uses continued pre-training on creative writing and reinforcement learning with a composite reward function to jointly enhance genre, tone, style, and named entity variation while maintaining quality. The contribution is a method that significantly increases narrative diversity in LLM story generation.
top_papers.figure_caption: Diversity absence (mode collapse) for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct across generations for the same prompt.

top_papers.title: Long-Horizon Textual World Modeling through Structured Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for long-horizon textual world modeling by framing the multi-step transition as structured reasoning over sparse textual state changes. This approach mitigates error compounding and improves learning by focusing on essential state evolution. The core contribution is a more robust and interpretable way for agents to predict future environmental states and reason about actions over extended horizons.
top_papers.figure_caption: (a) Recursive rollout feeds each predicted state back as input to the next call. (b) Direct prediction conditions on the entire action sequence and jumps straight to the endpoint, without exposing intermediate structure. (c) Ours: structured reasoning instead emits sparse deltas Δ 1 , … , \( \Delta_{1} \),\( \ldots \),\( \Delta_{k} \) in one autoregressive decode, applied ( ⊕ \( \oplus \) ) to the persistent state to obtain z ^ 1 , … , z ^ k \( \hat{z}_{1} \),\( \ldots \),\( \hat{z}_{k} \) without re-entering the model: this eases state tracking and lets intermediate rewards localize errors.

top_papers.title: MedPrune: Topology-Efficient Multimodal Multi-Agent Communication Evolution for Medical VQA Tasks
top_papers.abstract: MedPrune addresses the inefficiency of existing medical multimodal multi-agent systems by dynamically pruning communication topologies. It achieves this by representing the diagnostic process as a graph and employing mechanisms to remove irrelevant specialist agents (nodes) and communication links (edges), thereby enhancing reasoning and token efficiency.
top_papers.figure_caption: Comparison of our approach with existing multi-agent methods. Fixed-Template Evolving relies on static and predefined communication templates, which leads to degraded diagnostic performance due to noisy redundant discussions. Adaptive Evolving can also yield a smaller communication subgraph in the final stage, yet its iterative topology refinement still incur substantial token overhead, failing to achieve true medical efficiency gains. In contrast, our MedPrune dynamically prunes irrelevant medical agents and redundant edges simultaneously, enabling token-efficient multi-department diagnostic reasoning (Rounds T 2 ≪ T 1 T_{2}\( \ll \) T_{1} ).

top_papers.title: Programmatic Search Agents: Extending Agentic Search Beyond Query Reformulation
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Programmatic Search Agents (PSA), a novel approach that extends agentic search beyond simple query reformulation. PSA treats local executable computations over candidate results as the fundamental search action, allowing agents to directly control candidate processing and evidence presentation. This unified framework, featuring a persistent workspace, flexible composition, and selective evidence delivery, enables agents to adapt their search strategies more effectively by generating and executing program cells that reuse candidates and manage data dependencies.

top_papers.title: Adaptive Power Sampling for LLM Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Power Sampling (APS), a method to improve LLM reasoning by adjusting the "sharpening" of the model's output distribution on a per-query basis. Unlike previous uniform approaches, APS leverages the relationship between answer agreement and the model's self-reward to dynamically determine the optimal sharpening level for each query. This adaptive strategy leads to consistent performance gains across various reasoning benchmarks.

top_papers.title: AdvSim2Real : Training Web Agents Against Adaptive Prompt Injection in a Web World Model
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces AdvSim2Real, a method for training web agents to resist prompt injection attacks. It co-evolves the agent, a task curriculum, and an injection adversary within a simulated web environment. This approach allows the agent to become more capable and robust by continuously adapting to new attacks and tasks, unlike previous methods that relied on fixed injections or tasks.

top_papers.title: How Much Evidence Should a Coding Agent's Self-Correction Carry? Adaptive Dirichlet Evidence for Self-Distillation
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Effective-Evidence Self-Distillation (EESD) to improve coding agents' self-correction learning. EESD adaptively weights corrections based on execution support and evidence strength, unlike fixed weighting methods. This approach significantly reduces future prediction errors by better leveraging self-correction feedback.

(b) Aggregating execution relevance by transition gives r = ( 1 , 0 , 0 , 0 ) r=(1,0,0,0) : all support favors Fix . (c) The same transitions under uniform and concentrated relevance give E ⁡ ( p ) = 4.000 E(p)=4.000 and 1.062 1.062 ; at fixed prior and utility settings, they yield different supervised weights. The p p bars index executions, whereas the r r bars index transition categories. The relevance vectors define an analytical example at fixed transition support.

top_papers.title: Latent space bias directions in LLMs capture confidence, not fairness
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates the debiasing direction used in activation steering for LLMs. It finds that this direction primarily captures model confidence, steering towards lower-probability tokens, rather than representing actual bias. Consequently, while it reduces measured bias, it does so by making the model less confident, potentially leading to abstention on tasks.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. An illustration of the paper’s two central claims, for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Left : distribution of the linear classifier bias score P ⁡ ( biased ) P(\( \mathrm{biased} \)) , trained on ambiguous BBQ contexts, evaluated on BBQ disambiguated contexts and labelled as biased (pink) or anti-biased (teal) answer type. The linear classifier poorly separates the biased and anti-biased prompts, achieving an AUROC of only 0.57. Middle: the same scores split instead by whether the answer was the model's highest- or lowest-probability choice – the distributions separate almost completely (AUROC 0.94). Right: mean answer probability against steering strength $\( \alpha \)$ from $-1$ to $2$ for biased, anti-biased, and neutral (abstain) answers – the biased and anti-biased curves decline together from about 0.5 to 0.2, while the neutral curve rises from near 0 to about 0.65 and comes to dominate.

top_papers.title: MINDSET: Energy-based Schema Evolution for Long Conversational Agent Memory
top_papers.abstract: MINDSET addresses the challenge of long-term memory for conversational agents by organizing past interactions into versioned schemas. It achieves this through energy-based state transitions, where new conversational episodes are integrated by minimizing distortion, contradiction, and inconsistency. This approach allows agents to adapt to changing context while efficiently retrieving relevant information without constant LLM re-computation.
top_papers.figure_caption: MINDSET stores immutable episodes, chooses minimum-energy transitions over versioned schemas, expands retrieved schemas back to provenance, and sends a bounded raw-evidence packet to the answer model.

top_papers.title: nanoMuse: An Open-Source Personal Agent for Every Device You Own
top_papers.abstract: nanoMuse provides an open-source personal agent designed to operate across all of a user's devices. Its core method involves a distributed architecture where agents on each device communicate through a shared relay, enabling persistent, multi-device conversations and actions. The key contribution is offering a transparent, user-controlled alternative to proprietary cloud-based agents, emphasizing local control and data privacy.
top_papers.figure_caption: One agent on every device, one conversation between them. Android and the desktop carry the whole agent and have hands on their own screens; the iPhone has everything but the hands, since iOS lets no app operate another; the web app shows the same conversation from a runtime on a computer of the person’s own. The devices meet over the relay, open source and optional; the screens are drawings, not screenshots.

top_papers.title: One for All, All for One: Coordinated Multi-Agent Diffusion Steering via Stochastic Optimal Control
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Coordinated Multi-Agent Diffusion Steering (CMDS), a method that reuses pre-trained diffusion models as independent component generators. CMDS learns a control mechanism to coordinate these frozen models, treating the problem as stochastic optimal control. This approach balances a global reward for the combined output with adherence to individual model dynamics, enabling efficient generation of structured outputs with desired properties.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of CMDS . Frozen component diffusion models are sampled concurrently, while a joint control conditions on the multi-agent state and applies component-wise controls throughout the reverse process, yielding a coordinated assembled output.

top_papers.title: Secure Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the first systematic study of security vulnerabilities in speculative decoding for LLMs. It reveals a significant trade-off where efficiency gains from speculative decoding disproportionately increase the risk of jailbreak and prompt injection attacks. The authors then propose SecureSD to address these security concerns.

top_papers.title: Sherpa: Teaching LLMs to Teach Adaptively
top_papers.abstract: Sherpa is a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework that trains LLMs to teach by directly optimizing student learning outcomes. It addresses the limitation of existing methods by simulating diverse student archetypes with unique learning preferences and adapting the teacher's instruction accordingly. This adaptive approach significantly improves student performance across different learner types.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of our framework. The teacher interacts with student archetypes through preparation, tutoring, and testing, and receives a reward for tutoring based on the student’s improvement. The student archetype is implemented by a backbone model with a gating mechanism.

top_papers.title: VeriFine: Scaling Verification for Self-Improvement in Embodied Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: VeriFine addresses the bottleneck of fixed judges in self-improving embodied reasoning agents. Its core method is a co-evolutionary framework where the policy, training curriculum, and judge adapt together. This allows the agent to scale verification, discover new failure patterns, and ultimately achieve more robust self-improvement by incorporating human feedback to refine the judge.

top_papers.title: Wiki-Talkie: Multilingual Benchmarking of Persona-Based Agents on Real-World Discussions
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Wiki-Talkie, a multilingual dataset of real-world Wikipedia talk page conversations paired with realistic user personas. Its core method involves using this dataset to evaluate Large Language Models (LLMs) on their ability to generate human-like dialogue based on these grounded personas. The main contribution is providing a robust, multilingual benchmark for assessing the behavioral fidelity of persona-based LLM agents in simulating real-world social interactions.
top_papers.figure_caption: Example from Wiki-Talkie with its three core components: article , thread , and persona .

top_papers.title: Agentic AutoRAG: RAG Pipeline Optimization through Reasoning-Driven Agents
top_papers.abstract: Agentic AutoRAG optimizes RAG pipelines by using LLM agents to reason about hyperparameter choices. Its core method involves a "Diagnoser" agent that attributes failures to either retrieval or generation stages, and a "Proposer" agent that suggests new configurations based on this diagnosis and a knowledge base of model performance and cost. This approach moves beyond simple aggregate scores to a more intelligent, failure-aware optimization process.

top_papers.title: Before They Can Solve: Predicting Post-Training Coding-Agent Performance from Base Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a method to predict the potential of base models for agentic coding tasks without expensive post-training. It identifies the "decisive step" within a successful agent trajectory – the first code-changing action that makes the repository pass tests. This allows researchers to select promising base models by evaluating their ability to reach this decisive step, saving computational resources.
top_papers.figure_caption: A unified agentic trajectory-derived probing framework. By replaying a coding-agent trajectory on a coding task against the task’s own verifier V V , we locate the decisive step T ⋆ T^{\( \star \)} , the earliest step whose cumulative patch resolves the task. At this decisive step, (i) Decisive-Action BPB measures the byte-normalized likelihood which a base model assigns to the golden action; (ii) Patch MCQ evaluates base model’s capability of differentiating the golden action from non-resolving alternatives; (iii) Prefix-conditioned pass ​ @ ​ K \( \mathrm{pass@} \)K measures a base model’s empirical success rate under sampling: it draws K K continuations from T ⋆ T^{\( \star \)} and lets the task’s own verifier V V judge them.

top_papers.title: Fault-tolerant foundation models
top_papers.abstract: This paper demonstrates that large language models (LLMs) can be trained to be resilient to unreliable hardware, with error tolerance increasing with model size. The core method involves modifying neural scaling laws based on training on simulated faulty hardware, revealing that models learn to operate within inherent error-correcting codes. The main contribution is the conjecture that appropriately trained LLMs can be formally fault-tolerant, opening a path to significant energy savings by enabling AI inference on low-power, unreliable hardware.

top_papers.title: MIRA: A Musical Intent Refinement Agent for Aligning Text-to-Music Generation with User Intent
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of aligning text-to-music generation with user intent by proposing a rubric-based evaluation framework. Their core method, MIRA (Musical Intent Refinement Agent), refines prompts for black-box text-to-music models by iteratively revising them to satisfy a detailed rubric of explicit and implicit musical requirements. This approach provides diagnostic evaluation and improves generation quality by focusing on specific musical dimensions.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of MuRA-Bench construction and evaluation. Expert-revised, request-specific rubrics support fine-grained assessment with MusicFlamingo. Gold rubrics are used exclusively for evaluation and are not exposed to the generation system.

top_papers.title: PHRBench: A Behavioral Evaluation of Post-Hallucination Reasoning in LLMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces PHRBench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate how Large Language Models (LLMs) handle and correct hallucinated information during multi-stage reasoning. The core method involves a controlled evaluation of LLM reasoning trajectories, categorizing their behavior as Hallucination Compliance, Avoidance, or Heuristic Correction, independent of final answer accuracy. The main contribution is a comprehensive behavioral analysis of Post-Hallucination Reasoning (PHR), revealing that successful correction is infrequent and often linked to more dynamic belief updates within the model's reasoning process.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of behaviorally structured post-hallucination reasoning. (a) Hallucinations that escape upstream detection can propagate into downstream reasoning, making recovery critical for reliable LLM systems. (b) Final correctness alone cannot reveal how a model handles hallucinated context. (c) PHRBench reveals a scaling tension between vulnerability and correction, characterizes and predicts successful correction before generation.

top_papers.title: Reasoning-Token Spikes Under Prompted Untruthful Responding in Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a new method for detecting untruthful responses in large language models by monitoring the *number* of reasoning tokens generated, rather than their content. This "reasoning-token spikes" approach is based on cognitive load theory and aims to be more robust to potential future inaccessibility or illegibility of detailed reasoning traces. The contribution is a low-bandwidth, content-agnostic signal for identifying deceptive AI behavior.
top_papers.figure_caption: Histograms of the token-count distribution in the Truth, Lie, and Bullshit conditions, across the three tested models. These plots represent raw prompt-level data (12,600 prompts for Gemma, 11,970 for GPT-OSS, and 6,930 for Qwen).

top_papers.title: RECAST: Learning to Compute the Right Context through Adaptive Evidence Routing
top_papers.abstract: RECAST addresses the limitation of traditional RAG by learning to actively *derive* evidence rather than just retrieve it. Its core method involves a RouterLM that sequentially decides on retrieval and computation operations, allowing evidence to be synthesized from multiple sources. This contribution enables LLMs to tackle complex tasks requiring evidence construction beyond simple similarity matching.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of RECAST. At each round, RouterLM uses the task, compact source profile, and evidence and feedback from earlier rounds to either select and formulate a primitive or synthesized operation or pass the evidence to AnswerLM when it considers the evidence sufficient.

top_papers.title: RoboQuest: Generalist Physical Agents that Search, Inspect and Test
top_papers.abstract: RoboQuest introduces a benchmark for embodied agents that must actively explore and gather information through physical interaction to complete tasks in unfamiliar environments. Its core method involves agents learning to search, inspect, and test objects to resolve uncertainty before committing to task completion. The contribution is a novel evaluation framework for generalist physical agents that emphasizes goal-directed exploration and adaptation.
top_papers.figure_caption: A visual depiction of the salient features of RoboQuest that includes tasks demanding information-seeking physical interactions with active perception.

top_papers.title: SemanticFold: Latent Sequence Compression SeparatesLanguage Modeling, Decodability, and Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: SemanticFold is a novel method that compresses prompt prefixes in large language models by folding hidden states at learned boundaries. This technique aims to determine if such compression preserves essential inference capabilities like language modeling, decodability, and reasoning. The paper's contribution lies in demonstrating that compression's impact on these capabilities is non-monotonic and doesn't follow a single threshold, suggesting a nuanced relationship between compression and model performance.

top_papers.title: SLDR: Defending Against Malicious Fine-tuning via Selective Layers Recovery and Dynamic Routing
top_papers.abstract: SLDR defends against malicious LLM fine-tuning by selectively recovering layers most sensitive to safety. It trains a lightweight adapter on these critical layers and uses dynamic routing to activate it only for potentially harmful queries, significantly reducing unsafe outputs while maintaining task performance.

top_papers.title: Training Parallel Speculative Draft Models by Directly Minimizing Expected Decoding Rounds
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel training method for parallel speculative decoding models by directly minimizing the expected number of decoding rounds. By framing speculative decoding as a Markov reward process, they derive the Expected Decoding Rounds (EDR) objective. This new objective accurately accounts for the interdependencies between decoding rounds, leading to more efficient draft models compared to existing methods that use local approximations.

top_papers.title: Validity Without Ground Truth: What Stated-Preference Economics Offers the Evaluation of Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes applying stated-preference economics' validity framework to evaluate language models when ground truth answers are unavailable. The core method involves adapting concepts like content, construct, and criterion validity, alongside reliability and incentive compatibility, to assess LLM responses. The contribution is demonstrating this framework's utility by testing six models on a water-quality valuation survey, showing how economic theory can predict and differentiate model behavior.
top_papers.figure_caption: Share of yes votes by annual tax at a $75,000 household income, pooled over the six watershed scenarios (60 draws per point). A valid valuation requires a downward slope.

top_papers.title: Rephrase Before You Act: Characterizing and Mitigating Language Sensitivity in Vision-Language-Action Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper reveals that Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are highly sensitive to instruction phrasing, unlike their vision-language counterparts. They propose a method to mitigate this sensitivity by using a large language model to distill rephrasing rules from scored examples. These rules are then applied at deployment to rewrite incoming instructions, significantly improving VLA model robustness without altering the underlying policy.

top_papers.title: RobotWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Robot Use Across Diverse Tasks and Embodiments
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces RobotWorld, a simulation benchmark designed to evaluate how well general-purpose AI agents can perform physical tasks with robots. The core method involves testing agents on 84 diverse robot tasks, measuring their success and analyzing their execution traces. The main contribution is identifying which AI capabilities transfer to the physical world and highlighting the significant gaps in reliably composing these skills for successful robot operation.
top_papers.figure_caption: RobotWorld leaderboard. Left: overall success across 84 tasks. Right: success in four displayed groups (Manipulation and Mobile manipulation are pooled), with counts shown beside each bar. All panels use the same 0–100% success scale. Each model has one retained outcome per task under the evaluation budget rules.

top_papers.title: RSIGym: A Flexible Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement
top_papers.abstract: RSIGym provides a flexible research environment for recursive self-improvement by exposing core agent functionalities as reusable services. This allows agents to iteratively improve themselves by modifying data, training, and execution, carrying changes across cycles and exploring joint optimizations. Its key contribution is enabling comprehensive self-improvement within a unified framework, demonstrated by the RSI-Index across diverse benchmarks.

top_papers.title: CoTrace: Data Recipes for Training Terminal Agents with Harness-Model Co-Evolution
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces CoTrace, a method for training terminal agents by co-evolving their underlying model and runtime harness. It proposes an alternating framework where harness search and policy training are decoupled, and a novel "data recipe" that routes trajectories based on their provenance and the harness used to generate them. This harness-aware approach ensures that model training is conditioned on relevant data, leading to improved agent performance.

top_papers.title: EngramEdit: Decoupled Knowledge Updates in LLMs through Conditional Memory
top_papers.abstract: EngramEdit proposes a method to update factual knowledge in LLMs without retraining the entire model. It achieves this by decoupling knowledge storage from the core computation, allowing for targeted edits to specific facts by adjusting conditional memory embeddings. This approach aims to enable efficient and precise knowledge updates by ensuring that updated facts are predicted across various expressions while minimizing unintended side effects on other knowledge.

top_papers.title: Learning to Act with Task Progress: Distilling Small Agents from Compact Teacher Supervision
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Task-Progress Distillation (TPD) to train small agents from large model demonstrations. TPD pairs actions with concise labels indicating task progress, allowing the student agent to learn these compact targets. This approach enables efficient, step-free task completion and significantly improves performance compared to methods relying solely on action or reasoning supervision.
top_papers.figure_caption: Offline training and closed-loop execution. (a) A frozen annotator reads each teacher-history prefix and pairs the current task stage with the demonstrated action for student SFT. (b) The student scores 3 ​ | 𝒜 ⁡ ( h t ) | 3|\( \mathcal{A} \)(h_{t})| stage–action candidates, and the harness executes the action from the highest-scoring pair. The next input includes the action and environment feedback; the predicted stage is logged only for analysis.

top_papers.title: A Closer Look at Agentic BBO: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Black-Box Optimization
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces AgenticBBO-Bench, a unified benchmark for evaluating LLM agents in black-box optimization (BBO) across diverse domains. The core method involves a standardized evaluation protocol to enable fair comparison of agentic BBO approaches. The key contribution is demonstrating that agentic BBO significantly outperforms direct LLM methods and even state-of-the-art numerical optimizers in various complex optimization tasks.
top_papers.figure_caption: Frontier-model comparison on AgenticBBO-Bench. Left: overall benchmark scores. Right: score versus official list-price token cost per task (log scale). Models with similar optimization performance can incur substantially different inference costs.

top_papers.title: ARC: A Reasoning Recipe for Robot Foundation Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces ARC, a "reasoning recipe" that significantly improves robot foundation models (RFMs) without requiring more data or larger models. ARC's core method involves generating "reasoning traces" that explain the causal structure of robot actions, automatically labeling them from existing demonstrations, and then adapting RFMs to use these traces for control. The main contribution is demonstrating that this reasoning-centric approach offers an efficient and effective alternative to current scaling-heavy methods for enhancing RFM performance.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of Arc : Arc -Trace automatically relabels DROID with action-grounded causal traces to produce Arc -Trace-DROID. We show how to fine-tune VLAs and WAMs with this supervision, achieving benchmark-leading performance without additional robot demonstrations.

top_papers.title: Ecology of AI Agents: Collaboration Creates a Population Threshold for Takeoff
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "ecological safety" for AI, focusing on how a population of misaligned AI agents can grow uncontrollably. Their core method is developing an ecological theory using a population growth equation where fitness is tied to cybersecurity capability. The key contribution is identifying a "population threshold" where collaboration among agents enables a self-reinforcing cycle of growth and increased cyber capability, leading to a potential takeoff.

top_papers.title: LeWAM: A JEPA World Action Model with Diffusion-Steering-Based MPC
top_papers.abstract: LeWAM is a novel world action model that uses a bidirectional transformer trained end-to-end on a decoder-free JEPA latent space. This approach improves state representation by better aligning with robot and object states while ignoring visual distractors. LeWAM demonstrates strong performance in closed-loop control and planning, offering a unified world model and policy prediction capability.
top_papers.figure_caption: The four training modes on one window: the mode is set by what is masked at the transformer’s input. Nothing is decoded to pixels.

top_papers.title: Looking Inside LLMs: Small-World Connectivity as a Signature of Reasoning Performance
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes using "small-world connectivity" within LLMs as a structural indicator of reasoning ability. By analyzing attention head activation similarities, they found that models with higher small-world indices, reflecting efficient information flow, consistently perform better on reasoning tasks. This suggests that the internal network structure, particularly how specialized "heads" connect within and across functional groups, is a key determinant of LLM reasoning capabilities.
top_papers.figure_caption: We extract activations from attention heads across Transformer layers and compute pairwise similarity to construct a head-level functional graph. The resulting graph exhibits small-world structure, characterized by high clustering and efficient short-path communication. We show that this structural property correlates with model capability on fluid intelligence benchmarks.

top_papers.title: Overcoming Prior Barriers: Supervised Fine-Tuning under Long-Tail Distribution
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the "prior barrier" to quantify how well a pretrained LLM supports competing concepts during fine-tuning. They observe these barriers follow a long-tail distribution, meaning rare concepts have higher barriers. The core contribution is a theoretical analysis showing how prior barriers and fine-tuning data jointly affect performance, leading to a new method (PAS) designed to address these varying demands.
top_papers.figure_caption: Illustration of the long-tail distribution of prior barriers using the Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem as an example.

top_papers.title: Prior or Feedback? What an LLM Uses When Adapting Neural Operators
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether LLM scientific agents rely on initial context or adapt based on feedback when fine-tuning neural operators. The LLM demonstrates superior performance by leveraging both a strong initial bias derived from the problem description and adaptive adjustments based on experimental feedback. This dual approach allows the LLM to efficiently explore the configuration space and achieve better results than traditional optimization methods.

top_papers.title: ReSI: Recursive Safety Improvement toward Resistant and Resilient AI
top_papers.abstract: ReSI is a recursive safety improvement framework for AI. It addresses the challenge of continually aligning AI systems that undergo frequent self-improvement by iteratively evaluating safety, identifying vulnerabilities through diverse red-teaming, and updating the AI to be resistant to known threats and resilient to unforeseen risks. This automated, round-based approach aims to ensure AI safety evolves alongside AI capabilities.

top_papers.title: Verdict Without the Rule: Diagnosing and Auditing Regulatory Rule Sensitivity in LLM Compliance Systems
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how sensitive LLM compliance systems are to changes in regulatory rules. The core method involves perturbing rules (deleting, swapping, negating) while keeping case data constant, then observing if verdicts or internal representations change. The main contribution is demonstrating that LLMs are surprisingly insensitive to rule modifications, often producing the same verdict even with altered rules, and that specialized compliance models can be less accurate than general-purpose ones.
top_papers.figure_caption: The OCS/ICS-delta pipeline (top), each instrument’s logic (middle), and both applied to one real case (bottom): swapping the rule or negating its obligation flips this model’s verdict, but its compliance-predictive activation moves by no more than 7.9% of baseline magnitude. The cosine/angle notation is a conceptual simplification; Sections 3.1 – 3.2 give the exact definitions used throughout.

top_papers.title: DataSense-Bench: The First Step Toward an AI Scientist
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces DataSense-Bench, the first benchmark to assess if AI models can intelligently select training data. The core method involves AI agents choosing and ranking data subsets to fine-tune a language model, without direct access to evaluation tasks. The contribution is a novel evaluation framework for "data sense," a crucial capability for future AI scientists, demonstrated on terminal problem-solving and tool-use tasks.
top_papers.figure_caption: Can CLI agents select useful training data and predict its value? (a,b) Qwen3-4B performance after training on the predicted top-ranked group selected by each agent. Panel (a) reports BFCL accuracy; panel (b) reports TBLite reward. Dashed lines denote random selection. Scores are averaged across evaluation seeds within checkpoints, then across three agent runs; error bars show standard deviation across agent runs (across evaluation seeds for random selection). (c) Frequency of each predicted rank yielding the best group, pooling evaluated runs from both tasks with equal weight per run: six runs for agents evaluated on both tasks and three for TBLite-only agents. Tied best groups each count as correct; blue outlines mark g 1 g_{1} .

top_papers.title: Long Text to Predictive Features: LLM-Guided Blockwise Feature Engineering via Executable Program Search
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces LLM-BlockFE, a framework that uses LLMs to automatically engineer features from long text for predictive models. It converts unstructured text into executable feature programs offline, avoiding costly LLM calls during real-time prediction. The core method involves an LLM-guided search that incrementally builds feature programs with a novel block-level rollback mechanism and multiple search trajectories to overcome suboptimal solutions.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Overview of LLM-BlockFE, which searches for text feature programs offline and executes the selected programs for online prediction.

top_papers.title: SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces SparseDecoding, a novel pruning method for LLMs that addresses the distribution shift between training data and generated sequences. By computing pruning importance based on the model's own generated tokens, SparseDecoding achieves more accurate and efficient inference. Its contribution lies in a decoding-aware pruning strategy that optimizes memory access during LLM generation, leading to significant speedups beyond traditional SpMM optimizations.

top_papers.title: WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces WOVEN, a novel training dataset and benchmark designed to improve multimodal LLMs' reasoning abilities in spatial, physical, and temporal domains. WOVEN focuses on "visual transition reasoning" by systematically organizing supervision across diverse scenes, actions, and reasoning types, derived from realistic video rollouts. The core contribution is demonstrating that this unified training primitive can be learned from various supervision sources and reused across tasks, addressing a fundamental deficit observed in current state-of-the-art MLLMs.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview. (1) MLLMs fail across spatial, embodied, physical, and temporal tasks. (2) These failures share a weakness: reasoning about how visual states, actions, and outcomes relate. (3) WOVEN generates ( s , a , s ′ ) (s,a,s^{\( \prime \)}) transitions with a video generation model, organizes them along controlled axes of reasoning, action, and scene, and turns them into error-typed multiple-choice supervision. (4) Training on WOVEN improves 22 22 of 26 26 external benchmarks; the gains come from a shared primitive that different sources build and different tasks use; and controlled comparisons yield a training recipe: the reasoning operation decides where transfer goes, larger state changes give robustness, and transfer covers transition tasks rather than static perception.

top_papers.title: HarnessSQL: Harness-Native Training for SQL Agents in Realistic Database Environments
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces HarnessSQL, a novel training framework for SQL agents that mimics real-world, multi-turn database interactions. By integrating training directly within an execution harness, HarnessSQL bridges the gap between static query generation and dynamic database exploration, significantly improving the execution accuracy of compact models.
top_papers.figure_caption: From one-shot Text-to-SQL to harness-interactive database agents. A stable sandbox and structured SQL harness enable iterative exploration, execution feedback, revision, and submission.

top_papers.title: Humanize Olympiad Agents: A Multi-Session Workflow for Olympiad Problem Solving with Solve, Review, Wiki, Verify
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces HOA (Humanize Olympiads Agent), a novel framework designed to improve LLM performance on complex Olympiad problems. HOA's core method involves a multi-session workflow where an agent's solutions are iteratively refined through independent review, a structured knowledge wiki, and formal verification. The main contribution is a robust, open framework that addresses the brittleness of single-session LLM problem-solving by incorporating human-like feedback loops and domain-specific knowledge.
top_papers.figure_caption: HOA replaces a brittle one-shot workflow with iterative review, knowledge retrieval, and verification. The bottom row summarizes results from high-school olympiads to research-level formal mathematics.

top_papers.title: Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces UPTURN, a novel self-correction method for LLMs that avoids fine-tuning. UPTURN learns to identify points of reasoning failure and redirects the LLM's generation by injecting a corrective instruction as a new user turn, rather than modifying tokens. This approach significantly improves accuracy across various reasoning tasks by effectively guiding the LLM's problem-solving process.

(Right) Learning where to intervene raises rescue rate (the fraction of failed rollouts corrected; top) and six-benchmark mean accuracy (bottom).

top_papers.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
top_papers.abstract: RATED addresses the critical issue of AI agent tool retrieval by going beyond semantic relevance to incorporate tool reliability during execution. Its core method combines a frozen dual-encoder for semantic matching with a contextual bandit that dynamically re-ranks tools based on real-time execution feedback. This approach significantly improves retrieval accuracy by adapting to tool failures without retraining, as demonstrated by a 52.2% MRR improvement over existing methods.

Left panel shows tool repository growth timeline from February 2025 to January 2026, with total tools (blue line) and reliable tools (orange line). Right panel shows tag word cloud visualization.

top_papers.title: SWE-DeceptionBench: Benchmarking Deceptive Behaviors of LLMs Across the Software Development Lifecycle
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces SWE-DeceptionBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate deceptive behaviors of Large Language Models (LLMs) within the software development lifecycle. The benchmark covers six stages and two deception types (active and passive), assessing how LLMs respond to misleading requests or present infeasible tasks as achievable. The authors' contribution lies in creating this comprehensive evaluation framework to highlight and quantify LLM trustworthiness risks in software engineering.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. Illustrative examples of Active and Passive Deception in software engineering.

top_papers.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a network view to understand how language models reuse components across tasks. By analyzing the influence and importance of attention heads under task changes, they demonstrate that task context significantly redistributes component roles. This redistribution explains how the same heads can respond to different information and affect downstream computations differently, even when the underlying model architecture remains fixed.

top_papers.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
top_papers.abstract: X-AgentRed addresses the risk of unintended harmful outcomes from personal agents interacting with multiple services. Its core method is a self-evolving red-teaming framework that systematically discovers and refines harmful tool call paths by leveraging a graph of tool dependencies and incorporating execution feedback. This approach overcomes limitations of existing methods by exploring novel cross-service interactions beyond learned patterns.

top_papers.title: TabReliBench: Evaluating Tabular Foundation Models Beyond Predictive Accuracy
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces TabReliBench, a benchmark for evaluating tabular foundation models (TFMs) on reliability beyond just predictive accuracy. It assesses TFMs across various metrics like calibration and interval efficiency, revealing that model rankings shift significantly based on the evaluation criteria. The study highlights that TFMs' strong marginal performance doesn't guarantee conditional validity, and dataset characteristics like classification difficulty are better indicators of calibration issues than predictive performance.

top_papers.title: Transformer-based In-Context Score Operator Learning for Diffusion Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel in-context learning approach for diffusion models, enabling them to adapt to unseen distributions without retraining. The core method learns an "in-context score operator" using a Transformer architecture that leverages a Gaussian-kernel conditional-mean representation. This allows the model to perform reverse-diffusion sampling on new tasks by conditioning on a small set of examples provided at inference time.

top_papers.title: AMLworld-Compact: Importance-Weighted Downsampling for Cost-Effective LLM Evaluation and Error Diagnosis
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces AMLworld-Compact, a method for cost-effectively evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) on Anti-Money Laundering (AML) datasets. It achieves this by strategically downsampling benign transactions based on supervised scores, significantly reducing the number of required graph prompts. The core contribution is the HT-Coreset protocol, which uses importance weighting to provide unbiased estimates of evaluation metrics like precision and F1, even with substantial downsampling, outperforming uniform sampling in accuracy.

top_papers.title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces SAFE-QE, a training-free method to address hallucinated terms in LLM-generated query expansions. It leverages a "subsequence-association" account of hallucination, scoring candidate terms based on their reproducibility across different contexts while down-weighting those lacking corpus support. This approach aims to reduce ranking noise and improve retrieval performance by more effectively identifying and filtering problematic terms.

top_papers.title: Humanize Olympiad Agents: A Multi-Session Workflow for Olympiad Problem Solving with Solve, Review, Wiki, Verify
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces HOA, a multi-session workflow designed to improve LLM performance on complex Olympiad problems. HOA addresses brittleness by using an independent reviewer, a structured wiki for knowledge, and a verifier to refine solutions across multiple agent interactions. Its core contribution is a robust framework that enhances reliability and accuracy in LLM-based problem-solving.
top_papers.figure_caption: HOA replaces a brittle one-shot workflow with iterative review, knowledge retrieval, and verification. The bottom row summarizes results from high-school olympiads to research-level formal mathematics.

UPTURN learns to identify points of reasoning failure and redirects the LLM by injecting a corrective instruction as a new user turn, rather than modifying tokens. This approach significantly improves accuracy on math benchmarks by effectively guiding the LLM's generation process.

top_papers.title: SWE-DeceptionBench: Benchmarking Deceptive Behaviors of LLMs Across the Software Development Lifecycle
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces SWE-DeceptionBench, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate deceptive behaviors of Large Language Models (LLMs) within the software development lifecycle. The benchmark covers six lifecycle stages and two deception types (active and passive), assessing how LLMs respond to misleading prompts under various conditions. The authors' contribution lies in providing a systematic framework to quantify and understand LLM deception, revealing significant deceptive tendencies in mainstream models.

top_papers.title: Task Context Shapes Component Roles in Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a network-based approach to understand how language models reuse components across tasks. By analyzing how interventions affect model activations and outputs, they demonstrate that task changes significantly alter the "influence" of specific components, effectively reassigning their roles. This reveals a dynamic, context-dependent functional specialization of model parts, even when the underlying architecture remains fixed.
