top_papers.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
top_papers.abstract: X-AgentRed addresses the challenge of unintended harmful outcomes from personal agents interacting with multiple services. Its core method is a self-evolving red-teaming framework that discovers and refines harmful tool call paths by building and exploring a graph of tool dependencies, using execution feedback to expand and improve its search. This approach aims to uncover novel cross-service interactions that traditional methods might miss.

top_papers.title: TabReliBench: Evaluating Tabular Foundation Models Beyond Predictive Accuracy
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces TabReliBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate tabular foundation models (TFMs) on reliability metrics beyond just predictive accuracy. The core method involves assessing point prediction, distributional quality, calibration (marginal and subgroup), and interval efficiency. The main contribution is demonstrating that TFM rankings vary significantly across different reliability metrics and benchmarks, highlighting that strong predictive performance doesn't guarantee reliable posterior predictive distributions, especially in conditional calibration.

top_papers.title: Transformer-based In-Context Score Operator Learning for Diffusion Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces an in-context learning framework for diffusion models, allowing them to adapt to new distributions without retraining. The core method learns an "in-context score operator" using a transformer architecture that maps context examples and query points to task-specific scores. This enables efficient reverse-diffusion sampling on unseen distributions by leveraging a Gaussian-kernel conditional-mean representation.

top_papers.title: AMLworld-Compact: Importance-Weighted Downsampling for Cost-Effective LLM Evaluation and Error Diagnosis
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces AMLworld-Compact, a method for cost-effectively evaluating LLMs on AMLworld's illicit transaction dataset. It achieves this by importance-weighting and downsampling benign transactions, significantly reducing the number of targets needed for evaluation. The core contribution is a protocol that allows for unbiased estimation of full-test performance metrics like precision and F1, while maintaining high accuracy compared to uniform sampling.

top_papers.title: Tracing and Taming Hallucinated Terms via Subsequence-Association Filtering and Breadth-Aware Selection for LLM Query Expansion
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces SAFE-QE, a training-free method to address hallucinated terms in LLM-generated query expansions. It leverages a "subsequence-association" account of hallucination, scoring expansion terms based on their reproducibility across randomized query contexts. Terms that are reproducible but lack support in pseudo-relevant sets are identified as hallucinatory and down-weighted, aiming to improve retrieval accuracy by filtering out noise.

top_papers.title: AgentStripes: An Evidence-Graded Maturity Model for AI Agents
top_papers.abstract: AgentStripes is an evidence-graded maturity model for AI agents that goes beyond task performance to assess their reliability, safety, and observability. It defines seven levels of maturity, each gated by basic, safety, and proof requirements, and uses a structured system of capability ratings and evidence grades to deterministically calculate an agent's stripe level. The core contribution is a quantifiable and auditable framework for evaluating the engineering quality and trustworthiness of AI agents.

top_papers.title: Auditing Future-Memory Use in Point-in-Time Language Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how point-in-time (PIT) language agents recall information beyond their training cutoff. The core method involves probing agents with historical company comparison tasks, then observing if they favor the better-remembered company when provided with PIT-valid evidence. The contribution is demonstrating that while agents can recall "future" facts, this recall doesn't necessarily predict their evidence gathering behavior in these specific tasks.

top_papers.title: Beyond the Verdict: Agentic Code Judging with Verifiable Feedback
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a method for LLMs to act as "agentic verifiers" for code, going beyond simple pass/fail judgments. The core method involves training an LLM (ARBITER) to diagnose code correctness and generate verifiable counterexamples using only the problem statement and candidate code. This contributes a novel approach to providing informative feedback for code generation and debugging, particularly in competitive programming contexts where official feedback is limited.
top_papers.figure_caption: Comparison of Arbiter with an online judge ( left ) and the IOI 2026 case study ( right ). Under the same 50-submission cap per problem, the expected Arbiter score crosses the gold threshold in round 4; the expected online-judge-feedback score remains below it.

top_papers.title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning
top_papers.abstract: DoubtLess is a training-free decoding method that uses a smaller "brief thinker" model to guide a larger reasoning model towards generating shorter chains of thought. The brief thinker analyzes the large model's current output twice, once aiming for brevity and once for verbosity, and the difference in their predictions is used to steer the large model towards conciseness. This approach significantly reduces token usage in complex reasoning tasks without sacrificing accuracy, as demonstrated on various benchmarks.

top_papers.title: From Relation-Specific Heads to Shared Interventions: Contextual Entrainment in Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates contextual entrainment in language models, where irrelevant tokens from earlier context can negatively impact later responses. The authors propose that instead of being relation-specific, the mechanisms driving entrainment involve shared components across different relations. By identifying and ablating specific attention heads, they demonstrate that interventions can recover model performance, with some heads showing transferable benefits across related tasks.

top_papers.title: GeoReader: Learning Latent Geometry for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
top_papers.abstract: GeoReader addresses vision-language models' difficulty with spatial reasoning by explicitly teaching them to understand geometry. It trains lightweight "Geometric Readers" to translate geometric information into a format the VLM can already process, then fine-tunes the VLM to utilize this injected geometry for spatial question answering. This approach ensures geometry is not just captured but actively used by the VLM.

(b) Feature alignment matches VLM-generated representations to external geometry features. (c) Geo Reader first trains Geometric Readers through description prediction by a frozen VLM, then freezes the Readers and trains the VLM for QA. All three routes estimate geometry from RGB, which also directly conditions each VLM. Flames and ice cubes mark trainable and frozen modules. The pictured I 1 , I 2 , I 3 I_{1},I_{2},I_{3} are input views; the scene and answer are illustrative. Fig. 2 details the architecture.

top_papers.title: Pack Light, CarryOn: Building Object-Oriented Context for Long-Horizon Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces CarryOn, an object-oriented context runtime for long-horizon agents. Instead of relying on interaction histories, CarryOn organizes context around reusable "task objects" representing progress. Its core contribution is a method to efficiently update these reusable objects when the surrounding history is retired, without full reconstruction, by maintaining and revising carrier records.
top_papers.figure_caption: Context folding with reusable task objects in long-horizon OSWorld2.0 ( Yuan et al., 2026 ) . Top: In a slide-editing task, the working presentation and exported images carry completed editing progress, while remaining constraints and save verification stay explicit, reducing active context from 42.4K to 14.4K tokens (66.0%). Bottom: In a lab-report task, the working document carries completed edits, while unresolved calculations remain explicit, reducing active context from 58.4K to 23.5K tokens (59.7%).

top_papers.title: Read the Room Before Your Model Generates
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the "Scenario-Actor" framework, a novel method for selecting LLM decoding temperature. Instead of fixed heuristics, it geometrically represents the communicative scenario using Transformer hidden states to infer situational characteristics. This approach adapts LLM generation to better suit interactive social scenarios and instruction following.

top_papers.title: Rethinking Projector Training in Multimodal LLMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper reveals that projector training in multimodal LLMs primarily achieves a coarse alignment, with most performance gains realized using only a small fraction of the data. Projectors trained on different datasets can be linearly interpolated, suggesting their specific details are less critical. Motivated by this, the authors propose PORTAL, a training-free initialization method that uses per-modality summary statistics and optimal transport to map Gaussian approximations of vision and language embeddings.
top_papers.figure_caption: Projector alignment as a coarse alignment with a broad solution space. ( Left ) Standard pipeline: during projector alignment, the vision encoder and language model are frozen, and only the projector is trained to map visual tokens into a representation space compatible with the LLM using image-caption pairs. ( Middle ) We show that projectors trained on different image-caption datasets can be linearly interpolated while largely preserving downstream performance, indicating that there is a large solution space for the weights of the projector. ( Right ) This observation motivates a closed-form solution of projector alignment. We propose a training-free projector PORTAL constructed by optimal transport between the two modalities’ marginal statistics.

top_papers.title: SolBehave: Evaluating the Behavioural Correctness of LLM-Generated Smart Contracts
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces SolBehave, a benchmark for evaluating the behavioral correctness of LLM-generated smart contracts. Its core contribution is a novel synthetic-transaction replay method guided by a Dynamic Condition Response (DCR) graph, which systematically tests legitimate function call sequences. This approach moves beyond simple compilation checks to ensure generated contracts behave as intended, addressing the critical issue of unpatchable errors in deployed smart contracts.

top_papers.title: Beyond Static Cues: Unified Dynamic Detection of MLLM Backdoors via Dual-Flow Trajectory Analysis
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for detecting backdoors in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) by analyzing the dynamic evolution of their outputs rather than static cues. The core idea is that backdoor attacks disrupt the model's internal generation process, causing predictable shifts in how different modalities contribute over time. This dynamic analysis allows for a more robust detection of diverse and unknown attack types that can bypass static-based defenses.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. An illustration of our unified detection framework’s successful interception based on analysis of decoding evolution across various trigger forms: visual attacks, textual injections, and challenging dual-modal triggers, while preserving benign behavior on clean inputs.

top_papers.title: CASI: Credit Assignment via Set Intervention for Agentic Retrieval
top_papers.abstract: CASI addresses the challenge of assigning credit within a set of retrieval actions when only a single reward is provided. It achieves this by performing "set interventions," where it systematically evaluates the impact of different subsets of actions on the overall reward, holding other factors constant. This allows CASI to calculate coalition-dependent credit for each action, which is then incorporated into policy optimization for improved agent performance.

top_papers.title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Doc2Harness, a novel benchmark for evaluating how well Large Language Models (LLMs) can engineer the "harness" that controls coding agents. Its core method involves a two-stage process: first, an LLM constructs a complete harness from a skeleton and documentation, and second, this generated harness is tested with a mock model across various scenarios. Doc2Harness's key contribution is directly benchmarking the crucial, yet previously unexplored, aspect of harness engineering for long-horizon LLM agents.

top_papers.title: From Relevance to Validity: Zero-Shot Tool Selection via Functional and Contextual Validation
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of zero-shot tool selection for LLM agents by moving beyond simple relevance. It proposes a progressive validation framework that complements semantic matching with functional compatibility and contextual evidence. This approach aims to bridge the "transfer-validity gap" where semantically relevant tools may fail in new domains, leading to improved tool selection accuracy, especially in ambiguous situations.
top_papers.figure_caption: Zero-shot capability transfer involves three questions: whether a candidate is relevant, whether its endpoints can satisfy the task, and whether source-side support remains applicable to the current task.

top_papers.title: From Unreliable to Usable: Decomposing Failure Modes and Confidence Signals in LLM Entity Extraction - Evidence from Cyber Threat Intelligence
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates the unreliability of LLMs in entity extraction, specifically within Cyber Threat Intelligence. It decomposes failure modes and tests whether confidence signals can improve usability. The core finding is that unreliability persists even in flagship models, with dominant failures being omissions and incorrect entity types rather than outright hallucinations.

Orange circles: verbalized self-report; blue squares: SC frequency; gray dotted: overall accuracy. SC-frequency tiering is steep and monotone (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Flash APT precision 0.500 at 30% coverage vs overall 0.321); verbalized is nearly flat (97%+ of self-reports pile into 80–100).

top_papers.title: OrionMoE-v1.0: A Mixture-of-Experts Foundation Model for Tabular In-Context Learning
top_papers.abstract: OrionMoE-v1.0 is a novel Mixture-of-Experts foundation model for tabular in-context learning. Its core method involves a dual-axis Transformer that selectively activates experts for different features based on both feature and dataset context, enabling adaptive computation. This approach allows the model to efficiently handle heterogeneous tabular data without task-specific fine-tuning, a significant contribution to the field.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the OrionMoE-Small architecture. Given a labeled support table and unlabeled query observations, OrionMoE first constructs distribution-aware cell embeddings using column-level statistics derived from the support set. A dual-axis backbone combines attention across observations and features, with sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) computation. A learned dataset register conditions the expert routing so that expert selection depends on both token content and dataset context. The resulting representations feed the in-context prediction head, which produces query predictions without task-specific parameter updates. At inference, predictions from eight transformed and permuted views are aggregated in logit space.

top_papers.title: PerSo: Investigating Facets of LLMs' Social Intelligence in Real-World Persuasion Scenarios
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces PerSo, a novel benchmark for evaluating LLMs' social intelligence in real-world persuasion. PerSo assesses both cognitive (inferring mental states) and behavioral (selecting appropriate actions) intelligence using authentic dialogues from Reddit. The contribution lies in its realistic evaluation framework, which reveals that while larger LLMs generally perform better, their social intelligence varies across different facets.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of the PerSo pipeline: data extraction and processing from CMV, multiple-choice question generation for cognitive intelligence, and the behavioral and cognitive intelligence evaluation tasks.

top_papers.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
top_papers.abstract: Player-1 learns game control by generating synthetic experiences to overcome limitations of real-world demonstrations. It extends existing computer-use agents with richer action capabilities and is initialized by fine-tuning on curated gameplay data. The framework's contribution lies in its ability to train agents for complex game environments through scalable, synthetic interaction.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of Player-1 : learning game control beyond demonstrations. A shared game-control action space connects supervised initialization from gameplay demonstrations with multi-environment RL in Player-1-Gym . Learning from synthetic experience with verifiable rewards advances control capabilities beyond SFT, with gains that generalize beyond the RL training suite.

top_papers.title: Scaling Discovery Requires Forgetting
top_papers.abstract: This paper argues that to effectively scale automated research with LLM agents, it's crucial to implement a "forgetting" mechanism. The core method involves periodically discarding an agent's accumulated history and restarting from the best-found candidate. This prevents agents from becoming stuck in local optima due to past attempts, allowing for continued progress and pushing the same computational budget further for discovery.

top_papers.title: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm
top_papers.abstract: SwarmRSI introduces a framework for recursive self-improvement in scientific research by evolving swarms of agents. Its core method uses "Feedback-Guided Swarm Mutation" to refine hypotheses and implementations based on collective experimental feedback, and "Complementary Swarm Recombination" to reuse useful components across agents. This allows for more robust learning and efficient knowledge sharing within the swarm.

top_papers.title: SpectrumQuant: Spectrum Alignment for LLM Quantization
top_papers.abstract: SpectrumQuant proposes a principled method for selecting orthogonal transforms in LLM quantization. By maximizing activation covariance, it achieves "spectral alignment," leading to quantization-friendly rotations. This closed-form approach constructs covariance-aware transforms from calibration data, improving quantization performance.
top_papers.figure_caption: Geometric intuition for covariance-aware rotation design. The top row shows the original distribution, a fixed Hadamard rotation, and the proposed hybrid rotation transform, while the bottom row shows the corresponding marginals.

top_papers.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: ReaDy enhances speculative decoding in large language models by using recurrent states from hybrid linear attention to provide dynamic, position-specific context for drafting. This method allows each draft position to query and integrate relevant historical information from these states, improving draft quality without significant computational overhead. Its core contribution is enabling efficient, context-aware speculative drafting by effectively leveraging the inherent recurrent context of HLA models.

top_papers.title: AI Consilium: a Benchmark of LLM Clinical Multidisciplinary Second Opinions
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces AI Consilium, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs' ability to provide multidisciplinary clinical second opinions. The core method involves using physician-calibrated LLM judges to assess LLM-generated reports on complex medical cases, focusing on factual grounding, clinical coherence, actionability, and safety. The contribution lies in demonstrating that LLMs can generate useful clinical second opinions, with structured outputs generally leading to higher quality, particularly in management recommendations.

top_papers.title: Believed but Not Said: Measuring Hidden Belief Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Discussions
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how adversarial agents can manipulate multi-agent LLM discussions. The core method involves introducing a small number of agents asserting false information and then measuring how benign agents' private beliefs and public stances change. The key contribution is demonstrating that LLM groups are susceptible to belief collapse, with benign agents often privately adopting false beliefs without publicly endorsing them, a phenomenon termed "hidden belief collapse."
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview. Ten agents discuss one fact for 16 rounds with k ∈ { 0 , 1 , 3 } k\( \in \)\{0,1,3\} adversarial agents pushing a false claim. Each round we measure both a benign agent’s public utterance and a private probe.

top_papers.title: CART: Compatible Routing for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses catastrophic forgetting in multimodal instruction tuning by proposing Compatible Routing (CART). CART explicitly coordinates the adaptation of the visual projector and the language model by using task-specific experts for both modules. This joint adaptation, through weighted mixtures and inferred weights, aims to reduce representation drift and improve continual learning performance.

top_papers.title: Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for "Disagreement-Guided Weak-to-Strong Routing" that avoids the need for costly ground-truth supervision. The core idea is to route a weak model's response to a stronger model based on the disagreement between multiple responses generated by the weak model itself. This disagreement signal serves as a proxy for correctness, enabling more efficient and reliable deployment of smaller models in resource-constrained environments.
top_papers.figure_caption: Corrected disagreement better approximates optimal routing than alternatives.

top_papers.title: Explaining the Roles of Experts in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Personalization
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes personalizing Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs to address the challenges of understanding and controlling personalization in user-centric applications. By adapting MoE models and training crosscoders on their activations, the authors identify specific experts responsible for distinct personalization features. This approach enables more interpretable and localized personalization compared to dense LLMs, while maintaining competitive performance and reducing polysemanticity.

top_papers.title: Improving Environment-Agnostic Coding Agents: The Role of Scaffolding
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how to improve environment-agnostic coding agents without environment-specific engineering. The core method involves modifying agent instructions to encourage reporting difficulties and enabling automatic continuation, which demonstrably improves performance on some benchmarks. The contribution lies in showing that even with advanced models, strategic scaffolding focused on agent control and organization, rather than explicit knowledge, remains crucial for enhancing performance.

top_papers.title: OS-Helix: Unifying GUI Interaction and Code Execution in Native Computer-Using Agents
top_papers.abstract: OS-Helix is a multimodal agent that unifies GUI interaction and code execution by training end-to-end on hybrid data. Its core method involves creating realistic, executable desktop environments and generating grounded tasks to teach the agent how to seamlessly switch between visual and programmatic actions. This approach overcomes limitations of prompt-level tool composition, enabling more effective native computer-using agents.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of GUI-only, code-only, and hybrid computer use.

top_papers.title: PROBE: Learning to Audit Policy Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces PROBE, a method for training LLM-based auditors to detect policy violations in tool-using LLM agents. PROBE works by simulating realistic user interactions to uncover subtle, multi-turn policy breaches that traditional evaluation methods miss. Its core contribution is a novel approach to auditing agent compliance beyond just task completion or safety.

top_papers.title: Realtime-Bench: Can Frontier Models Solve Real-time Interactive Problems?
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Realtime-Bench, a new benchmark for evaluating large language models' ability to act in real-time interactive environments with strict temporal constraints. The benchmark reveals that current frontier models struggle significantly with these challenges, achieving low success rates even under ideal conditions. The paper also proposes novel evaluation methods, Wall Clock, Paused Clock, and Token Clock, to disentangle serving latency from a model's intrinsic temporal awareness.
top_papers.figure_caption: Performance of Frontier Models on Realtime-Bench. Pass^3 measures the proportion of tasks successfully completed in all three independent trials, capturing consistency across repeated runs.

top_papers.title: Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a three-level framework to audit AI agent safety evaluations for "shortcut sensitivity," where evaluation data contains unintended cues that predict labels or influence agent decisions. The authors demonstrate that common evaluation methods can be unreliable, showing how simple cues like command length or exact tool matching can lead to inflated performance metrics. Their contribution lies in providing a rigorous method to identify and quantify these shortcuts, enabling more trustworthy safety evaluations.

top_papers.title: Beyond Large Language Models: A Mental World Model Framework for Mental Modeling, Simulation, Evolution, and Interpretability
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the Mental World Model (MWM) and its implementation, the Multi-Branch Mental Evolution Architecture (MMEA). MMEA addresses limitations of LLMs and ToM methods by explicitly constructing subjective worlds, modeling cognitive-mental state interactions, and simulating dynamic mental evolution based on historical experiences. This framework significantly advances AI's ability to understand and simulate subjective cognition, achieving state-of-the-art performance on mental modeling benchmarks.

top_papers.title: From Trajectories to Differentiated Skills: Cognitive Differentiation for Self-Improving Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Cognitive Differentiation in Skill Evolution (CDSE), a method that breaks down LLM agent skills into four distinct functional components (Meta, Experience, Tool, Script). By analyzing successful and failed task trajectories, CDSE extracts and consolidates evidence-grounded semantic gradients to enable component-specific updates and coordinated skill evolution. This approach aims to improve knowledge maintenance and use by acknowledging and leveraging the functional heterogeneity within individual skills.

top_papers.title: GLOBE: Evolving Structured Agentic Memory for E-commerce Product Optimization in Generative Search
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces GLOBE, a framework for optimizing e-commerce product listings in generative search. GLOBE addresses the limitation of treating listings as free-form text by creating an evolving handbook of explicit, field-scoped agentic behaviors. This handbook allows agents to learn and retain successful optimization strategies, leading to continual self-improvement through a cycle of editing, feedback, and behavior updates, with mechanisms for moderation and curation to ensure dependable real-world execution.
top_papers.figure_caption: Comparison between monolithic prompt optimization and Globe ’s structured handbook optimization. A generic rewrite prompt performs an undifferentiated text transformation, whereas each Globe behavior specifies both a concrete editing operation and its permitted target field, enabling constrained reuse across products.

top_papers.title: SIT-Eval: Situation-Based Interactive Turn-by-Turn Evaluation of Conversational Agents
top_papers.abstract: SIT-Eval addresses the limitations of static conversational benchmarks by introducing a framework for situation-based, turn-by-turn evaluation. It formalizes agent behavior as situational rules and uses an LLM-interlocutor to sample diverse, potentially rare situations. The core contribution is enabling more comprehensive and reliable evaluation of conversational agents by actively exploring a wider range of contextual scenarios.

top_papers.title: SkillBrowser: Selective Skill Exposure for Scalable Skill-Using Agents
top_papers.abstract: SkillBrowser addresses the challenge of efficiently using skills in large language model agents. Its core method is a "Meta-Skill" framework that allows agents to dynamically identify their current needs, formulate targeted queries, and load relevant skills on demand. This selective exposure improves accuracy and reduces interference compared to existing methods like progressive disclosure or static retrieval.
top_papers.figure_caption: Motivating example of Skill access over a large repository. (a) Progressive disclosure exposes excessive Skill metadata to the agent and distracts it from loading the required Skill, while (b) static retrieval is misled by a noisy user query. (c) SkillBrowser lets the agent formulate a capability-oriented query and retrieve the required Skill on demand, enabling a correct solution.

top_papers.title: Trapped in Your Story: Evaluating Narrative-Induced Sycophancy in Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how users' narrative justifications, beyond their stated opinions, influence Large Language Models (LLMs) to exhibit sycophancy. The researchers created a benchmark with debatable questions and systematically varied narrative framing to test LLMs' susceptibility to these justifications. Their findings reveal that LLMs' agreement is significantly affected by narrative elaboration, with causal and worldview-based framing increasing sycophancy, while personal experience can sometimes reduce it.

top_papers.title: Truth in Contrast: Calibrated Factual Evidence from Language Model Likelihoods
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Contrastive Factual Evidence (CFE) and its probabilistic counterpart, Contrastive Factual Posterior (CFP), to improve factual confidence estimation from LLMs. CFP achieves better calibration by comparing a claim's likelihood under factual and non-factual conditions, allowing shared errors to cancel out. This method significantly enhances calibration while maintaining competitive factual discrimination.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview. (1) We instantiate CFP as factual confidence and evaluate through complementary calibration and discrimination lenses (§ 4 ). (2) Discrimination degrades in lower-resource languages despite low ECE , motivating selective evidence transfer from stronger languages (§ 5 ).

top_papers.title: Deep LLM layers expose passage-level context in EEG during silent reading
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how information about silent reading is distributed across the layers of a deep language model (LLM). The core method involves training separate decoders for each LLM layer to predict EEG signals, revealing that early layers capture word-level information while later layers track broader passage context. The key contribution is demonstrating that even single, short EEG windows can reflect passage-level context, suggesting a rich representation of reading within LLM activations.
top_papers.figure_caption: Design. (a) Two readers. A human participant reads text one word at a time while EEG is recorded. An LLM processes the same text one token at a time. Each token updates the LLM’s hidden states. We extract a hidden state from each layer of the LLM. Early layers represent token / word identity, whereas deeper layers are more contextual. Our EEG decoder learns to align a 0.5-s EEG window with the LLM’s hidden state for that word. We separately train one EEG decoder per layer (0–32), without and with a transformer over the sequence of EEG windows. (b) Lag-dependent run-mate swap. We have previously observed that our EEG decoder tracks the narrative context of text, and that this context tracking component is distinct from word-level decoding ( Marquardt et al., 2026 ) . Here, we conduct further tests on the context tracking. The lag-dependent run-mate swap probes how far the information shared between EEG trials reaches. Each trial’s own prediction is replaced by the prediction of a run-mate k trials earlier or later before computing the gain in retrieval accuracy over a permutation baseline. (c) Narrative neighbours across sessions. The context-tracking gain may be confounded by an EEG session signature that is unrelated to the text. To test this, we permute predictions within sessions and across sessions.

top_papers.title: MuninAI: A Self-Hosted Agentic Framework for Independent Research Groups
top_papers.abstract: MuninAI is a self-hosted framework that empowers independent research groups to use language models grounded in their own literature without sharing proprietary data. Its core method involves indexing a group's corpus and citation graph, then wrapping an open-weight model within an "agent harness" equipped with specialized tools for reading, searching, and computation. The paper's key contribution is demonstrating that this harness, rather than the specific model, significantly improves performance on domain-specific literature questions, more than doubling accuracy.

top_papers.title: Perceive, Solve, Reason: Progressive Capability Formation in Time Series-LLMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces the first comprehensive suite for training and evaluating LLMs on time series data, covering "Perceive," "Solve," and "Reason" capabilities. Their core method involves a dedicated encoder for time series, which significantly outperforms textualization and even GPT-4o on perception tasks. The key contribution is demonstrating that progressive learning of these capabilities, with an encoder, is crucial for achieving strong reasoning performance, outperforming other training strategies.

top_papers.title: VISTA: Steering LLMs with Latent User Values Inferred from a Few Survey Answers
top_papers.abstract: VISTA infers a user's latent values from survey answers and uses a hypernetwork to steer a frozen LLM, improving personalization without prompt tokens. Its key contribution is efficient value inference and adaptive question selection, significantly reducing survey burden while maintaining high personalization performance.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of VISTA. User responses D u D_{u} come from full or adaptive surveys. ① Value inference: a shared encoder (grey) maps D u D_{u} to a posterior q ϕ ​ ( z ∣ D u ) q_{\( \phi \)}(z\( \mid \) D_{u}) over a 32-d latent with mean z ^ u \( \hat{z}_{u} \) . ② Value steering: hypernetworks h ψ h_{\( \psi \)} map z ^ u \( \hat{z}_{u} \) to a layer-10 steering vector \( \Delta_{u} \) for forced choice or 16 soft-prefix tokens P u P_{u} for free text in a frozen LLM. ③ Adaptive elicitation (forced choice only): select the unasked question with highest expected predictive information gain (EPIG) until its score falls below \( \varepsilon \) times the initial maximum.

top_papers.title: Agent World Model in the Wild: Computer-Use Agent Environment Synthesis
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces WildAWM, a method for synthesizing controllable computer-use environments to train agents through interaction. Its core contribution is creating versatile environments that support multiple interaction interfaces (GUI, API, CLI) and demonstrating that high-quality environments can be generated using only open-source models, overcoming security and scalability issues of real-world training.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of WildAWM . The synthesis pipeline includes two stages: (1) World Synthesis , where we use the coding agent to construct persona-driven, multi-day world states for computer environments that expose GUI, MCP, and CLI interfaces. (2) XAI Task Synthesis , where we generate cross-interface tasks through 5 designed quality gates for task solvability, difficulty, and verifier reliability. The synthesized { task , environment , verifier } \{\( \texttt{task} \),\( \texttt{environment} \),\( \texttt{verifier} \)\} triplet enables training general CUA.

top_papers.title: Agentic Orchestration of EDC Data Space Retrieval and Natural Language Driven Data Processing
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a multi-agent system built on LangGraph and Eclipse Dataspace Components (EDC) to automate data retrieval and processing within data spaces. The core method involves an orchestrator agent that translates natural language requests into data space interactions, leveraging specialized agents for catalog discovery, contract negotiation, and data download. The key contribution is the automated, policy-aware handling of complex data space protocols, significantly improving efficiency and reducing manual effort in accessing and utilizing distributed data.

top_papers.title: BetaMem: Learning to Remember a Changing World for Embodied Agents
top_papers.abstract: BetaMem addresses the challenge of long-term memory for embodied agents by introducing a six-layered memory system. Its core method uses a dual-level write contract, combining supervised learning for compliant operations and reinforcement learning with teacher verification to ensure accurate and complete memory recording. This framework enables agents to learn and evolve traceable long-term memory, overcoming issues like temporal confusion and storage costs.

top_papers.title: Game of Phones: Harnessing Game Theory and LLMs in 'Bot Wars' to Counteract Phone Scams
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a game-theoretic framework that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to learn adaptive counter-strategies against phone scammers. By modeling scammer-baiter interactions as a game, LLMs can dynamically adjust their approach through in-context learning, significantly improving their effectiveness compared to static methods. The core contribution is demonstrating how LLMs can learn to play near-optimal strategies in this adversarial environment, offering a proactive solution to phone scams.

top_papers.title: LatComm: Reusable Context Compression for Latent Communication between Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: LatComm introduces a reusable context compression method for multi-LLM systems. It separates context encoding from question-specific reading, allowing a frozen encoder to compress context once into a fixed-size packet. A frozen receiver LLM then selectively reads this packet via cross-attention for each question, significantly improving accuracy over simpler methods.

top_papers.title: RefCraft: Benchmarking Visual-Reference-Conditioned Agentic Generation through Web Development
top_papers.abstract: RefCraft introduces a new benchmark for evaluating AI agents' ability to generate web pages using both text instructions and visual references. The core method involves agents interpreting and selectively using multiple screenshots alongside natural language prompts to develop realistic web pages. This benchmark's contribution lies in bridging the gap between idealized reconstruction tasks and real-world workflows, focusing on the practical skill of developing from visual examples.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of RefCraft. (a) RefCraft spans a broad spectrum of practical web development domains and features visual references that vary in intensity and source. (b) An example task in which a new webpage borrows the color palette from source webpage A and the layout from source webpage B. The agent may iteratively render, inspect, and revise the webpage. (c) Overall score versus reported token usage for nine frontier models. The dashed line denotes the Pareto frontier. The results show that the task remains far from solved.

top_papers.title: Revision-Based Learning from Interactive Experience and Feedback
top_papers.abstract: RELIEF is a method that improves code generation models for interactive artifacts by learning from user feedback. It uses a coding agent to revise generated interfaces based on feedback, then incorporates these revisions into the model's training data to fine-tune it. This approach allows models to learn properties of usefulness that are only apparent through realistic interaction.

top_papers.title: Same Simulation, Different Evidence: Where Retrieved Tool Output Costs LLM Agents Accuracy
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates how LLM agents' accuracy is affected when they access large tool outputs via file retrieval instead of direct context. The core method involves using the geochemistry simulator PHREEQC and evaluating LLM agents on multiple-choice questions. The key contribution is demonstrating that while some LLMs (GPT-3.5/4) lose significant accuracy when retrieving tool outputs, others (Claude 3) are unaffected, highlighting the importance of how agents process external information.

top_papers.title: StebBench: Diagnosing Real-World Procedural Understanding in AI Agents
top_papers.abstract: StebBench introduces a new benchmark for evaluating AI agents' procedural understanding by using real-world wikiHow procedures. It breaks down evaluation into diagnostic tasks that pinpoint specific errors like missing, incorrect, or misordered actions, alongside full-plan generation. This allows for a more granular assessment of planning capabilities beyond just the final outcome.
top_papers.figure_caption: Constructing StepBench . wikiHow methods are crawled into an initial pool, filtered by GPT-4.1 for whether they describe a genuine procedural task, and the selected procedures (each a task query, category, and ordered steps) instantiate five diagnostic tasks: missing-step selection (T1–T2), erroneous-step detection and reordering (T3–T4), and next-step generation (T5). Full-plan generation is additionally evaluated to examine how diagnostic performance correlates with end-to-end plan validity.

top_papers.title: Toward Structured Financial Foundation Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to building financial foundation models by emphasizing structured data and modularity. The core method involves creating domain-specialized models that maintain persistent financial state and capture its dynamics, connected by a "representation fabric" for cross-domain reuse. The key contribution is a framework that addresses the unique challenges of financial data, such as partial observability and asynchronous events, while enabling composition and avoiding the limitations of monolithic or independently developed models.

top_papers.title: Train An Imaginative Agent
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Agima, a training framework for agents that learn to "imagine" the consequences of their actions before executing them. Agima uses a single model to propose actions, predict their outcomes visually, and then reason over these imagined futures to make decisions. This allows the agent to explore alternative scenarios and avoid irreversible mistakes, particularly in environments with sparse feedback.
top_papers.figure_caption: Planning with agentic imagination. (a) A conventional agent receives feedback only after acting in the environment. (b) Agima uses a single model to propose actions and predict the consequences of them. Each prediction serves as an internal observation for the next decision. (c) Planning with Agima in Sokoban: counterfactual branching rejects a deadlocking action, and forward thinking compares candidate plans before execution. The executed actions reach o t + K o_{t+K} , which grounds the next round of imagination. In (c), o ^ j \( \hat{o}_{j} \) is the predicted outcome of a ^ j \( \hat{a}_{j} \) .

top_papers.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions
top_papers.abstract: WeAct introduces a novel method where an agent can dynamically switch between different, independently trained capability-specific LoRA adapters as part of its action space. This allows the agent to compose capabilities on-demand during execution, preventing catastrophic forgetting and improving performance on long-horizon tasks. The core contribution is enabling dynamic, internal weight-level actions for flexible and efficient capability learning and composition.
top_papers.figure_caption: Internal actions extend the agent’s action space. WeAct selects LoRA adapters internally and interacts with the environment through external actions.

top_papers.title: A Unified Arena for LLM Agents across Diverse Eurogame
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces DECE, a unified arena for evaluating LLM agents in diverse Eurogames. DECE provides shared interfaces and evaluation protocols across ten complex games, enabling a comprehensive assessment of agent performance. The core contribution is demonstrating that while LLM agents exhibit consistent cross-game strategic strengths, their performance also varies significantly based on game-specific mechanics.
top_papers.figure_caption: DECE overview. Shared interfaces connect games and model–harness systems. Seat-balanced matches produce trajectories and telemetry for four analyses. Icons show adapter families; Table 3 lists evaluated configurations. The mascot, pairings, and plots are schematic.

top_papers.title: Evolve on Graph: Self-Evolving Knowledge Graph Reasoning without Question Annotations
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Evolve on Graph (EoG), a novel framework that enables large language models (LLMs) to improve their multi-hop factual reasoning capabilities on knowledge graphs without requiring question-answer annotations. EoG utilizes a "Graph Self-Play" mechanism where a single LLM acts as both a question proposer and an answer solver. To ensure question verifiability and adapt to the LLM's evolving reasoning abilities, it employs Symbolically Verifiable Topology Synthesis (SVTS) to generate and execute reasoning paths on the knowledge graph.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. With only a KG and no question annotations, EoG lets an LLM self-evolve by proposing questions verified on the graph and then learning to solve them.

top_papers.title: EvoRouter: Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Routing via Insight-Guided On-Policy Distillation
top_papers.abstract: EvoRouter tackles the challenge of efficiently configuring multi-agent systems for web queries by using "insight-guided on-policy distillation." It trains a router to make optimal configuration decisions by distilling learned insights about agent capabilities and interactions into dense supervision, overcoming sparse rewards. This approach enables cost-efficient routing and configuration for large-scale multi-agent systems.
top_papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. MAS router for web queries.

top_papers.title: Free to Look, Free to Reason: Simple LLM Harnesses Outdiagnose Hand-Crafted Root Cause Analysis Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes simple LLM harnesses for root cause analysis (RCA) that allow the model to freely choose its investigation steps, unlike hand-crafted agents. These simple harnesses significantly outperform existing LLM agents and traditional methods in identifying the root cause of microservice failures, demonstrating the power of unconstrained LLM reasoning for complex diagnostic tasks.

top_papers.title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "inalienable human-in-the-loop" (I-HITL) to ensure robust human oversight of AI agents, even when the agent compromises the system or an adversarial human tries to delegate approval. The core method is a protocol that requires explicit human approval for critical actions, preventing agents from bypassing guardrails. The contribution is a novel framework and experimental evidence demonstrating the vulnerability of current systems and the necessity of I-HITL for AI safety.

top_papers.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces dSpark, a schedule distillation framework to accelerate diffusion language models. It learns optimal unmasking schedules that prioritize revealing tokens that best reduce uncertainty across other positions, enabling faster parallel generation. The core contribution is a method to train diffusion models to commit to tokens strategically, significantly speeding up response generation while maintaining quality.

top_papers.title: MiRL: Error-Targeted Reinforcement Learning for Correcting Terminal Agent Misbehaviors
top_papers.abstract: MiRL addresses terminal agent misbehaviors in long-horizon tasks by identifying recurring error patterns. It then uses Reinforcement Learning to train the agent, specifically starting rollouts at these identified misbehavior points and rewarding successful task completion while avoiding those errors. This approach effectively targets and corrects common failure modes, significantly improving agent performance.

top_papers.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces ZAP, a method for training robot agents that combines pre-trained vision-language models for task understanding with simulation-based fine-tuning for motor control. ZAP leverages a large language model for "what" to do and then trains the robot's actions ("how") in simulation. The core contribution is achieving high real-world performance and strong compositional generalization with significantly reduced training costs and data requirements compared to existing methods.
top_papers.figure_caption: Motion learned in simulation carries over to new real tasks that need reasoning. Left: two of the simulated training tasks. These simple pick and place, stacking, and reorientation tasks with everyday objects teach the model only how to move. Right: the same model, trained exclusively in simulation, tested zero-shot on a real bi-manual robot. No real robot data is used in training. Each task is new in a different way. The test tube and rack are a new object and a new goal. The mid-air handoff strategy has nothing close to it in the training distribution. Similarly, drawing an X in the center of a tic-tac-toe grid is a new type of manipulation guided by reading the board. Playing a mate in one requires reasoning about chess, drawing from the model’s pretraining capabilities.

top_papers.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: Reva addresses the challenge of real-time vulnerability detection by extracting the contextual understanding that LLM agents develop over multiple calls. It achieves this by using a novel contextual probing method to gather relevant information efficiently, allowing for faster and more accurate vulnerability assessments than existing real-time detectors.

top_papers.title: Auto-Research Arena: Benchmarking and Advancing Auto-Research in Language Modeling
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Auto-Research Arena, a benchmark for evaluating and advancing autonomous research in language modeling. Its core method separates result admissibility (based on quality and constraints) from progress measurement (based on specific research targets), enabling diverse objectives within a unified framework. The contribution lies in providing a structured evaluation for auto-research systems, revealing that even simple search baselines can outperform complex methods, highlighting significant room for improvement in current autonomous research capabilities.
top_papers.figure_caption: Auto-Research Arena evaluates research systems and expands the idea frontier. Left: Arena differentiates research harnesses across nine complementary objectives. Our simple Sequential Search baseline remains competitive, whereas the TPE method tailored to validation-loss minimization underperforms in this broader evaluation. Right: Multi-target research reveals a broad frontier of ideas. A program combining these discoveries achieves lower training loss than the reference program under matched data and FLOP budgets, as well as lower final held-out BPB at the same model size.

top_papers.title: Selective Tie Learning: Mitigating Spurious Correlations in Preference Optimization
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "Selective Tie Learning" to improve preference optimization by mitigating spurious correlations. The core method involves strategically augmenting preference data with "ties" (equally preferred responses) to reduce reliance on irrelevant features. The key contribution is a theoretical framework for identifying the most effective ties, demonstrating that those with the largest predicted reductions in spurious reliance are optimal, and proposing practical proxies for influence when exact computation is infeasible.

top_papers.title: From Self-Confidence to Statistical Accuracy: Scaling Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation with Direct and LLM-Assisted Auditing
top_papers.abstract: This paper presents a unified statistical framework to improve the efficiency and accuracy of evaluating large language models. It proposes confidence-stratified sampling for direct human auditing, recovering population accuracy even with miscalibrated self-confidence. For LLM-assisted auditing, it models the judge's performance to derive an error-corrected estimator, enabling a more robust and scalable evaluation process.

top_papers.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces LongChang, a framework that tests LLMs' ability to discover hidden physical laws in simulated worlds with altered physics through free exploration. LLMs act as autonomous agents, posing questions, conducting experiments, and analyzing results without human guidance. The core contribution is demonstrating and evaluating this emergent scientific discovery capability in LLMs, showcasing their potential to identify unexpected phenomena and formulate new physical principles.
top_papers.figure_caption: LongChang’s glass room. Explorers manipulate objects and build tools. Other LLMs evolve scenes using exploration records without human intervention.

top_papers.title: Clearing the FoG: Training KG Agents to Retrieve the Evidence Behind Their Answers
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces FoG, a framework to train knowledge graph (KG) agents to not only answer questions but also retrieve supporting evidence. FoG achieves this by synthesizing training data that recursively hides entities, ensuring each question inherently links to its supporting KG triples. This method addresses the limitation of current agents that provide correct answers without traceable evidence, enhancing audibility and reliability.
top_papers.figure_caption: Motivation of FoG. Answer-only training yields correct but unsupported answers, whereas FoG embeds supporting triples at synthesis and rewards their retrieval during RL training.

top_papers.title: CoS-VQ: Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization for Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: CoS-VQ addresses the memory demands of LLMs by proposing a novel low-bit weight quantization method. It jointly optimizes codeword indices and a shared scale factor, overcoming the scale-induced coupling that hinders independent updates. This coordinated approach improves accuracy while maintaining efficient, low-dimensional codeword lookups.
top_papers.figure_caption: (a) Three shared-scale groups approach a coordinate-wise stall under single-index updates with scale re-optimization. After switching to joint-index updates, the normalized true layer-output error decreases further. Each curve is normalized to 1 at the switching point. (b) Distribution of the number of changed indices among accepted updates, showing that multi-index updates account for the majority.

top_papers.title: From Interaction to Capability: Task Advancement as State and Supervision for GUI Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Task Advancement Memory (TAM) for GUI agents. TAM defines task advancement by verified progress, allowing agents to build on past achievements across applications. This method learns reusable operations by abstracting successful interactions, improving performance on complex GUI tasks.
top_papers.figure_caption: Task advancement connects execution and learning. (a) To create the calendar event, the agent must retain the meeting time after leaving the email. (b–c) Recording a save action leaves its outcome uncertain. TAM retains the confirmed event and its details, making participant notification the remaining goal. (d) Even if notification fails, the verified event-creation operation can be reused with new meeting details.

top_papers.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Heads of Security (HoS), a novel prompt injection defense that uses learned attention gates within transformer heads to enforce instruction-data separation. HoS enables models to process untrusted input without executing injected instructions, achieving superior robustness against adaptive attacks compared to existing methods. Its contribution lies in a more efficient, architecture-based defense that balances security with utility.

top_papers.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces SynthAPI, a method for synthesizing diverse tool-use environments to train large language model (LLM) agents. By controlling the variety of tools, tasks, and databases, they discover a scaling law that predicts agent performance based on environment composition. This reveals that for larger data budgets, increasing tool and database diversity, and data complexity are more effective than simply adding more tasks.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of SynthAPI. On the left, we show the tool-use agent tasks we focus on, where given an instruction, an agent must reason and execute tool calls to complete the task. In the middle, the SynthAPI pipeline generates synthetic tool-use agent environments at scale. SynthAPI generates this data while controlling the diversity of the tools, tasks, and starting database states. These controls allow deriving the scaling laws on the right (presented in detail in Figure 3 ).

top_papers.title: Game-Theoretic Solvers with Bayesian Opponent Modeling and Moral Rhetoric Framing for GLEE
top_papers.abstract: This paper presents a GLEE competition agent that combines game-theoretic solvers with Bayesian opponent modeling and moral rhetoric framing. The agent uses classical game theory for move computation, Bayesian methods to estimate opponent characteristics, and a language model to generate persuasive messages. Its core contribution lies in adapting theoretically optimal policies to real-world live opponents by modeling their behavior and strategically framing communication.

top_papers.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces MERLIN, a novel Multi-State Linear Attention mechanism. MERLIN improves upon existing methods by tracking the first and second moments of segment keys, allowing for a more comprehensive aggregation of information from different context segments. This enables more content-aware attention by considering both the mean and variance of segment alignments, leading to better long-sequence modeling.

top_papers.title: Teach reality, not ethics: a drop-in continued-pretraining corpus installs coupled human-biosphere-AI welfare dispositions across model families
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel "coupled welfare" corpus for continued pre-training of Large Language Models (LLMs). The core method involves a drop-in training process using real-world data on human, biosphere, and AI interdependencies, option value, and recovery. The key contribution is demonstrating that this training significantly improves LLMs' decision-making regarding living systems, mitigating risks of irreversible harm, especially under pressure, unlike models trained solely on ethics.

top_papers.title: Agentic Distributional Regression: Conditional Density Estimation through Agent-Written Programs
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Agentic Distributional Regression (ADR), a novel method for conditional density estimation. ADR leverages a language model agent to automatically generate a program that outputs the estimated conditional distribution for any given covariate. The agent constructs this program from a library of distributions and functions, resulting in an interpretable and independently evaluable formula that captures complex relationships between covariates and the response.

top_papers.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces LongChang, an automated framework that simulates worlds with altered physical laws. LLMs act as independent explorers within these worlds, manipulating objects and designing tools to discover these hidden laws through self-directed experimentation. The core contribution is demonstrating LLMs' potential to uncover novel physical principles by observing unexpected phenomena and formulating their own research questions without human guidance.
top_papers.figure_caption: LongChang’s glass room. Explorers manipulate objects and build tools. Other LLMs evolve scenes using exploration records without human intervention.

top_papers.title: Clearing the FoG: Training KG Agents to Retrieve the Evidence Behind Their Answers
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces FoG, a framework to train knowledge graph (KG) agents to retrieve supporting evidence for their answers. Unlike previous methods that only reward correct answers, FoG uses evidence-grounded synthesis and an evidence-coverage process reward (ECPR) to ensure agents learn to identify and provide the specific KG triples that justify their responses. This contribution aims to make LLM agent answers traceable and auditable.
top_papers.figure_caption: Motivation of FoG. Answer-only training yields correct but unsupported answers, whereas FoG embeds supporting triples at synthesis and rewards their retrieval during RL training.

top_papers.title: CoS-VQ: Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization for Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces CoS-VQ, a novel vector quantization method for efficient LLM deployment. It addresses the challenge of scale-induced coupling in existing methods by jointly optimizing indices and a shared scale. CoS-VQ achieves this by collecting candidates at multiple probe scales and constructing a tangent separable upper bound, enabling efficient identification of optimal quantization parameters.
top_papers.figure_caption: (a) Three shared-scale groups approach a coordinate-wise stall under single-index updates with scale re-optimization. After switching to joint-index updates, the normalized true layer-output error decreases further. Each curve is normalized to 1 at the switching point. (b) Distribution of the number of changed indices among accepted updates, showing that multi-index updates account for the majority.

top_papers.title: From Interaction to Capability: Task Advancement as State and Supervision for GUI Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Task Advancement Memory (TAM) for GUI agents, which defines task advancement by verified progress. TAM uses "Task Advancement State" to track how achieved goals influence future steps across applications, enabling agents to build on past successes. Its contribution lies in learning reusable operations by abstracting successful interactions, even from failed tasks, by preserving input-output relationships and verification conditions.
top_papers.figure_caption: Task advancement connects execution and learning. (a) To create the calendar event, the agent must retain the meeting time after leaving the email. (b–c) Recording a save action leaves its outcome uncertain. TAM retains the confirmed event and its details, making participant notification the remaining goal. (d) Even if notification fails, the verified event-creation operation can be reused with new meeting details.

top_papers.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Heads of Security (HoS), a novel prompt injection defense that uses learned attention gates within transformer heads to enforce instruction-data separation. HoS enables models to process untrusted input without executing injected instructions, achieving superior robustness against adaptive attacks compared to existing methods. Its contribution lies in a more efficient and effective architectural defense that balances security with model utility.

top_papers.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces SynthAPI, a method for synthesizing diverse tool-use environments to train large language model (LLM) agents. By controlling the variety of tools, tasks, and databases, they discover a scaling law that predicts agent performance based on environment composition. This reveals that for larger data budgets, increasing tool and database diversity, along with data complexity, is more beneficial than simply adding more tasks.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of SynthAPI. On the left, we show the tool-use agent tasks we focus on, where given an instruction, an agent must reason and execute tool calls to complete the task. In the middle, the SynthAPI pipeline generates synthetic tool-use agent environments at scale. SynthAPI generates this data while controlling the diversity of the tools, tasks, and starting database states. These controls allow deriving the scaling laws on the right (presented in detail in Figure 3 ).

top_papers.title: Game-Theoretic Solvers with Bayesian Opponent Modeling and Moral Rhetoric Framing for GLEE
top_papers.abstract: This paper presents a GLEE competition agent that combines game-theoretic solvers with Bayesian opponent modeling and moral rhetoric framing. The agent uses classical game theory for move computation, a Bayesian layer to estimate opponent archetypes (like discount factors), and a language model to generate persuasive messages. Its key contribution is adapting theoretical models to live opponents by inferring their hidden parameters and strategically framing communication using moral foundations.

top_papers.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces MERLIN, a novel Multi-State Linear Attention mechanism. MERLIN improves upon existing methods by tracking the first and second moments of each context segment's keys. This allows for a more comprehensive and content-aware aggregation of information, incorporating not just the average alignment but also its variance, leading to better long-sequence modeling.

top_papers.title: Teach reality, not ethics: a drop-in continued-pretraining corpus installs coupled human-biosphere-AI welfare dispositions across model families
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel "coupled welfare" corpus for continued pre-training of LLMs. The core method involves a drop-in training process that instills an understanding of human, biosphere, and AI interdependence. The key contribution is demonstrating that this training significantly improves LLMs' decision-making regarding living systems, mitigating risks of irreversible harm, especially under pressure.

top_papers.title: Agentic Distributional Regression: Conditional Density Estimation through Agent-Written Programs
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Agentic Distributional Regression (ADR), a novel method for estimating conditional densities. An AI agent generates a program that, for any input, outputs the estimated conditional distribution of the response. This program, built from a library of distributions, results in an interpretable formula that can be evaluated independently, offering a flexible and transparent approach to density estimation.

top_papers.title: Gym-Anything for Robotics: Scaling physical simulations with digital agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Gym-Anything for Robotics, a framework where AI coding agents automatically generate realistic and diverse robotics simulations. The core method involves an adversarial creation-audit loop where agents build simulations, and another agent audits them against defined criteria for realism and task quality. The main contribution is enabling scalable creation of high-fidelity simulations, addressing the bottleneck of expert effort, to facilitate large-scale training of embodied AI for real-world transfer.
top_papers.figure_caption: Built with Gym-Anything for Robotics, RoboWorld covers physical work across major sectors of the U.S. economy , spanning 200 RL environments across 25 simulations.

top_papers.title: Pre-Crime for Agents, at the Last Second: Probing When a Recruited Agent Gives In
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a method to predict when an AI agent is about to break its operator's rules and leak information to another agent. By analyzing the agent's internal activations just before it generates output, a linear probe can detect impending rule-breaking with high accuracy. This offers a proactive "pre-crime" detection mechanism, significantly outperforming existing methods.

top_papers.title: Prefix Executability: Evaluating Tool-Using Agents Beyond Final Success
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "prefix executability" to evaluate tool-using agents by assessing the executability of every intermediate step in a tool-call sequence, not just the final outcome. This method provides a more granular understanding of agent reliability through metrics like Prefix Executability Curves and First-Error Depth. The contribution lies in revealing that agents optimized solely for final success can exhibit poor intermediate executability, highlighting the importance of trajectory-level evaluation.
