top_papers.title: Retrieval as Traversal: Value-Indexed Memory for Stateful Long-Context Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a novel memory system for long-context agents that treats retrieval as a local traversal through an address space. Instead of re-searching the entire memory, it leverages the overlap between consecutive retrieval steps. The core contribution is a cost-regularized indexing objective that prioritizes preserving information value within local neighborhoods, encouraging complementary memories to be co-retrievable.

top_papers.title: SCARL: Sequence Confidence-Aligned Reinforcement Learning
top_papers.abstract: SCARL addresses a misalignment in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) where the policy's confidence in a response doesn't correlate with its reward. It proposes to "reshape" the reward signal by aligning the policy's confidence with the actual outcome. This ensures that confident successes receive stronger reinforcement and confident errors are corrected more effectively, leading to improved language model reasoning.

top_papers.title: TextSeal2: Distortion-Free LLM Watermarking with Copula Mixing and Memoryless Races
top_papers.abstract: TextSeal2 introduces a distortion-free LLM watermarking method that preserves output diversity and inference speed, even under speculative decoding. Its core innovation is merging multiple watermarking keys into a single virtual key using Gaussian copulas, allowing for robust detection without signal dilution. This approach also enables efficient verification during speculative decoding through a memoryless race mechanism.

top_papers.title: Understanding and Mitigating Role Spoofing in LLMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates "role spoofing" in LLMs, a vulnerability where models confuse the source of text based on style rather than explicit role labels. The core method involves analyzing how LLMs track conversational attribution, revealing they rely on both content and structural cues. The contribution is demonstrating the effectiveness of role spoofing attacks that combine fake structure and content, and proposing adversarial training as a mitigation strategy.

top_papers.title: VeriCUA: Verification as Agentic Exploration for Computer-Using Agents
top_papers.abstract: VeriCUA addresses the challenge of verifying computer-using agent (CUA) task completion by treating verification as an active exploration process. Instead of relying on static observations or limited program inspections, VeriCUA dynamically gathers evidence across different platforms and modalities. Its core contribution is a platform-agnostic framework that unifies online and offline verification through this agentic exploration, overcoming the limitations of partial views in existing methods.
top_papers.figure_caption: VeriCUA inspects the available environment or recording before constructing a rubric, then gathers evidence to verify its requirements.

top_papers.title: Rimuru: Unified Memory Management for Modern LLM Serving via Elastic Expert Offloading
top_papers.abstract: Rimuru addresses LLM serving memory strain by introducing unified memory management for heterogeneous tensors. Its core method is elastic expert offloading, which dynamically reallocates memory between model weights and attention states based on workload demands. This contribution significantly improves memory utilization and throughput, especially in resource-constrained environments, by breaking down rigid memory boundaries.

top_papers.title: Every Token Needs Its Own Teacher: Multi-teacher Adaptive On-policy Self-distillation
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes Multi-teacher Adaptive On-policy Self-Distillation (MTA-OPSD), a novel method for post-training large language models. Unlike previous approaches that use a single, fixed teacher, MTA-OPSD dynamically selects the most suitable teacher for each individual token within a response. This token-level adaptation, achieved through majority voting and KL-based selection from a pool of teachers, allows for more precise and effective distillation, leading to improved model performance.

top_papers.title: Multi-View MoE: Letting Every Router Shape Expert Computation
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Multi-View MoE, a novel approach to improve sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. It utilizes multiple independent routers to generate differentiated expert preferences, leading to more effective expert selection. By aggregating these preferences, the model can better shape expert computation and enhance overall performance within a fixed active-expert budget.

top_papers.title: rTaste: Do Research Agents Have Taste? Evaluating Early Stage Research Judgment
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces "rTaste" to evaluate whether AI models can exhibit "taste" in research, meaning they can judge the potential value of experiments before execution. The core method involves having AI agents propose and rank minimum viable experiments (MVEs) based on NLP papers, which are then executed and judged by human auditors. The contribution lies in demonstrating that while AI agents can generate valuable research ideas, their ability to consistently identify truly novel and impactful experiments is limited, and teamwork doesn't significantly improve this judgment.

top_papers.title: ShallowDefend: Harnessing Shallow Safety Alignment for Multi-Turn Defender
top_papers.abstract: This paper addresses the failure of current safety alignment in LLMs to handle multi-turn harmful requests. Their core method, Assess $\to$ Decide $\to$ Respond, involves the defender first assessing user intent, making an explicit safety decision, and then generating a response conditioned on that decision. The contribution is a more robust defense by intervening at the highest-leverage point – the initial decision – rather than just the surface response.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of our framework. At each turn, the defender assesses the user’s intent, commits to an explicit decision, and generates a response conditioned on that decision. For reward computation, we consider two options: an external reward model that judges whether the response is jailbroken, or a rule-based self-reward that checks the final turn’s committed label against the conversation’s ground-truth nature. RL gradients are applied only to the final turn.

top_papers.title: 4DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agents on Inverse Graphics of Dynamic Scenes
top_papers.abstract: 4DCodeBench is a new benchmark for evaluating AI agents' ability to perform 4D inverse graphics by generating executable code that reconstructs dynamic scenes from videos. The core method involves agents translating visual observations into compact representations of scene structure and dynamics, often requiring them to implement physical simulations. The contribution lies in providing a diverse set of real-world and synthetic videos to test this capability, revealing that current models struggle with complex dynamics despite strong static reconstruction skills.

top_papers.title: Credit Where It Matters: Dependency-Aware Policy Optimization for Terminal Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Dependency-Aware Group Policy Optimization (DepGPO) for reinforcement learning agents operating in terminal environments. DepGPO addresses the issue of irrelevant credit assignment by constructing a command dependency graph from execution traces. It then traces backward from task verification results to assign credit specifically to commands that directly influenced the outcome, thereby improving learning efficiency.

top_papers.title: CVE2AP: Automated Generation of PDDL-Encoded Attack Paths via Large Language Models
top_papers.abstract: CVE2AP automates the creation of formal attack path models in PDDL from natural language CVE descriptions. It leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) with structured prompting and an error-feedback loop to overcome the limitations of manual expert-driven modeling, enabling scalable and dynamic cybersecurity analysis.

top_papers.title: Do Large Language Models Know Colombian Law? A Reliability Benchmark for the Colombian Legal System
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel, expert-validated benchmark to assess the reliability of Large Language Models (LLMs) on Colombian law. The benchmark, comprising 1,042 questions across ten legal areas and three formats, reveals significant limitations: while LLMs can be relevant, their factual accuracy on free-text legal answers is consistently low (below 0.45), highlighting a critical gap in their current capabilities for legal applications outside the US.

top_papers.title: Jumping the Line: Exploiting Length Predictions in LLM Scheduling
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces JIL, an attack that exploits length predictions in LLM schedulers. JIL adds an adversarial suffix to requests, causing schedulers to underestimate their length and thus grant them higher priority. This manipulation leads to significantly faster completion times for adversarial requests.

top_papers.title: Measure Less, Know More: Self-Supervised Test-Time Feature Acquisition
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes ECHO-$k$, a self-supervised method for efficiently acquiring relevant features from multimodal data at test time. It leverages a foundation model's internal representations as proxy targets to learn a task-agnostic policy for selecting the most informative modalities, thereby reducing acquisition costs while improving downstream performance.

top_papers.title: Threat-Preserving Representation Sensitivity in Agent-Security Benchmarks
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces Threat-Preserving Representation Sensitivity (TPRS) to evaluate how benchmark representations affect LLM agent security evaluations. TPRS measures changes in attack success rate (ASR) when only the agent-visible representation is altered, keeping other factors constant. The study demonstrates that modifying tool names within benchmarks significantly impacts ASR, highlighting a crucial flaw in current security evaluation methods.

top_papers.title: When a Correct Reward Is Not Enough: Diagnosing and Guiding PPO in an Analytically Solved Broker-Trader Game
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) can effectively learn optimal strategies in a financial game with an analytical solution. The core method involves training a PPO agent to act as a broker in a broker-trader game, using a derived reward function. The contribution lies in demonstrating that while PPO can approach the optimal solution in simpler scenarios, it struggles to achieve accuracy in the presence of stochastic market noise, even when supervised learning confirms the actor's capacity.

top_papers.title: Divergence controls entropy in distillation
top_papers.abstract: This paper reveals that the choice of divergence function in distillation directly controls the student model's entropy. Specifically, forward KL divergence inflates student entropy, while reverse KL deflates it. This finding offers a new entropic perspective on distillation, explaining observed behaviors and highlighting divergence as an implicit entropy regularizer.

top_papers.title: FALCON: A Model and Dataset Agnostic Framework for Synthetic Data Generation for NL2SQL Pairs
top_papers.abstract: FALCON is a framework that generates realistic and ambiguity-aware synthetic NL-to-SQL data. It addresses the limitations of existing methods by producing complex queries that better reflect real-world challenges, using reserved-word SQL seeding and persona-based prompting. The framework's contribution lies in its ability to create high-quality, difficulty-preserving data cost-effectively, improving the robustness of NL2SQL models.
top_papers.figure_caption: Simplified architecture of the FALCON pipeline. It integrates systematic seeding, SQL and NL generation with CoT, and a multistage filtering process (Ambiguity, Reward, and Prompt-based), to produce high-quality NL-to-SQL pairs. To see a more detailed diagram of our pipeline, see Figure 6

top_papers.title: Balancing Memory Pathways: Analyzing and Improving Memory Utilization in Hybrid LMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper analyzes hybrid language models and finds they underutilize their recurrent memory pathways, relying too heavily on attention. The core contribution is a method to improve the coordination between these pathways, encouraging more balanced memory utilization and better performance by addressing this imbalance.

top_papers.title: Does AI Help Cyber Attackers or Defenders? Evidence from Nonpublic Vulnerabilities and Subsequent Attacks
top_papers.abstract: This paper evaluates AI models on their ability to generate exploits and repair vulnerabilities in non-public software environments. Its core contribution is providing evidence on whether AI aids attackers or defenders by testing models on unseen vulnerabilities, revealing significant variation in performance and highlighting that AI's impact is not uniform across different tasks and systems.

top_papers.title: A Society of Researchers: Designing Institutions for Populations of Autonomous Research Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes a "society of researchers" model for managing large populations of autonomous AI agents working on scientific tasks. The core method involves designing explicit institutions, inspired by human scientific communities, where agents compete for resources through proposals and reviews, overseen by a human governor. The contribution is a framework for organizing massive agent populations, enabling emergent, efficient scientific discovery, as demonstrated by a lab finding significant compute savings in language model pretraining.

top_papers.title: AI Safety Considerations for Agents With Limited Time to Act
top_papers.abstract: This paper argues that existing AI safety arguments often overlook the crucial role of the environment. It introduces theoretical bounds for agent-agnostic safety in partially observable, time-constrained environments, demonstrating that even a perfect agent cannot guarantee safety. The core contribution is highlighting that AI safety proofs must explicitly consider the environment and its associated safe actions alongside the agent.

top_papers.title: LAPT-Scale: Scaling Embodied Policies with Latent Action Pre-Training on Human Videos
top_papers.abstract: LAPT-Scale addresses the challenge of scaling robotic policies by leveraging large-scale human videos. Its core method involves pre-training a robot policy using "latent actions" extracted from human video transitions, which capture fine-grained motion dynamics. This approach significantly reduces the need for costly robot interaction data, enabling more generalist and capable embodied policies.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of LAPT-Scale. LAPT-Scale-LAM annotates egocentric human videos with continuous implicit actions. LAPT-Scale-Policy uses these annotations for human-video pre-training, followed by target-robot embodiment alignment and downstream post-training.

top_papers.title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces MC-EvoBench, a controlled Minecraft benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate embodied recursive self-improvement in agents. Its core method involves a fixed set of "evolution chains" where agents must demonstrate persistent, transferable capabilities by overcoming specific challenges. The key contribution is a robust evaluation framework that isolates true capability acquisition from confounding factors like resource carryover or initial failures.
top_papers.figure_caption: Evaluation mechanism of MC-EvoBench. A conventional benchmark records only whether an agent reaches the goal. MC-EvoBench also measures progress through the task graph, transfers only a declared experience artifact into a reset target world, and compares related, unrelated, and shuffled source conditions. We separate partial progress, physical carryover, and source-specific experience gains from improvements caused by favorable initial states or execution luck.

top_papers.title: Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates the run-to-run variance in semantic query processing, where LLMs judge individual data rows. The core method involves re-executing existing benchmarks and logging millions of model calls to quantify how much query results change across different executions, even at temperature 0. The key contribution is demonstrating that this variance, while seemingly small at the row level, can significantly impact overall query answers and system comparisons due to plan amplification, challenging the reliability of current benchmark evaluations.

top_papers.title: Your Discrete Graph Diffusion Model is Secretly Memorizing
top_papers.abstract: This paper reveals that discrete graph diffusion models (GDMs) secretly memorize training data, a phenomenon previously overlooked. The core method involves analyzing reverse diffusion trajectories conditioned on corrupted training graphs, demonstrating a strong bias towards reconstructing these specific training examples over novel test graphs. This "conditional memorization" emerges as a growing generalization gap, indicating that GDMs, despite appearing to generate novel graphs, are retaining and recalling information from their training set.

top_papers.title: Finite-Sample Guarantees for Fully Discrete Conditional Diffusion Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper provides the first finite-sample guarantees for conditional diffusion models trained with discrete steps. The core method aligns score training with the sampling grid, enabling joint analysis of statistical and discretization errors. This leads to theoretical bounds on the generated distribution's error, showing it scales favorably with sample size and model smoothness.

top_papers.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
top_papers.abstract: QTestBench is a novel framework designed to evaluate the effectiveness of LLM-generated quantum test suites. Its core method involves using independent benchmark checkers to validate tests, rather than treating the tests themselves as the ground truth. This approach allows QTestBench to assess how well LLM-generated tests can distinguish correct quantum code from faulty implementations, addressing a critical gap in current quantum software evaluation.

top_papers.title: Returning to Development States: When Full Sandbox Snapshots Help Coding Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes using Go-Explore-style search with full sandbox snapshots to improve coding agents' failure recovery. The core method involves restoring and branching from intermediate environment states, particularly those containing runtime information like databases and services, rather than restarting from scratch. The main contribution is demonstrating that this approach significantly boosts solve rates and efficiency, especially for complex coding tasks involving multiple interconnected services whose state is not easily reproducible from code changes alone.

top_papers.title: LAPT-Scale: Scaling Embodied Policies with Latent Action Pre-Training on Human Videos
top_papers.abstract: LAPT-Scale addresses the challenge of scaling robotic policies by leveraging large-scale human videos. Its core method involves pre-training a robot policy using "latent actions" extracted from human video transitions, which capture fine-grained motion dynamics. This approach significantly reduces the need for costly robot interaction data, enabling more generalist and capable robotic agents.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of LAPT-Scale. LAPT-Scale-LAM annotates egocentric human videos with continuous implicit actions. LAPT-Scale-Policy uses these annotations for human-video pre-training, followed by target-robot embodiment alignment and downstream post-training.

top_papers.title: MC-EvoBench: Auditing Experience-Driven Self-Improvement in Minecraft Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces MC-EvoBench, a novel Minecraft benchmark designed to rigorously audit the self-improvement capabilities of embodied agents. Its core method involves a controlled environment with registered "evolution chains" and task-state graphs, ensuring that agents must demonstrate genuine skill acquisition rather than relying on external resources or prior exposure. The contribution lies in providing a robust framework to isolate and measure persistent, transferable capabilities, crucial for advancing recursive self-improvement in AI.
top_papers.figure_caption: Evaluation mechanism of MC-EvoBench. A conventional benchmark records only whether an agent reaches the goal. MC-EvoBench also measures progress through the task graph, transfers only a declared experience artifact into a reset target world, and compares related, unrelated, and shuffled source conditions. We separate partial progress, physical carryover, and source-specific experience gains from improvements caused by favorable initial states or execution luck.

top_papers.title: Same Query, Different Answer: Run-to-Run Variance in Semantic Query Processing
top_papers.abstract: This paper investigates the run-to-run variance in semantic query processing, where LLMs evaluate individual data rows. The core method involves re-executing existing benchmarks and logging millions of LLM calls to quantify how much query results change across executions, even at temperature 0. The contribution highlights that this variance, amplified by query plans, can significantly alter final answers, impacting the reliability of current benchmark evaluations and system comparisons.

top_papers.title: Your Discrete Graph Diffusion Model is Secretly Memorizing
top_papers.abstract: This paper reveals that discrete graph diffusion models (GDMs) secretly memorize training data, contrary to prior beliefs. The core method involves analyzing reverse diffusion trajectories on corrupted training graphs, demonstrating a strong bias towards reconstructing these specific graphs over novel ones. The key contribution is identifying and naming this "conditional memorization," which emerges when the model is guided by corrupted training data and coincides with a widening generalization gap.

top_papers.title: Finite-Sample Guarantees for Fully Discrete Conditional Diffusion Models
top_papers.abstract: This paper provides the first finite-sample guarantees for conditional diffusion models trained on data and using a fixed number of discrete denoising steps. The core method aligns the score-training objective with the sampling grid, enabling joint analysis of statistical and discretization errors. This leads to theoretical bounds on the generated distribution's error and quantifies the necessary number of score evaluations, achieving improved convergence rates for KL and total-variation divergences.

top_papers.title: QTestBench: A Test Framework for Evaluating LLM-Generated Quantum Code
top_papers.abstract: QTestBench is a novel framework designed to evaluate the quality of quantum test suites generated by Large Language Models (LLMs). Its core method involves using independent benchmark checkers to validate LLM-generated tests, rather than treating the tests as the ground truth. The contribution lies in its ability to assess whether LLM-generated tests can effectively distinguish correct quantum code from faulty implementations, addressing a critical gap in current quantum software testing.

top_papers.title: Returning to Development States: When Full Sandbox Snapshots Help Coding Agents
top_papers.abstract: This paper proposes using Go-Explore-style search with full sandbox snapshots to improve coding agent performance. The core method involves restoring and branching from intermediate environment states, especially those containing crucial runtime data like databases and services. The main contribution is demonstrating that this approach significantly enhances solve rates and efficiency, particularly for complex, multi-service coding tasks where progress is not solely contained within code changes.

top_papers.title: AI-Driven Reproducibility and Analytical Robustness in Scientific Discovery
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces SEER-Repro, a benchmark for evaluating the reproducibility of scientific findings from the SEER cancer registry. The authors develop an AI agent capable of automatically reproducing a significant portion of published claims and assessing the robustness of medical findings by exploring alternative analytical choices. Their core contribution is demonstrating how LLM agents can automate and enhance the critical processes of scientific reproducibility and analytical robustness.

top_papers.title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
top_papers.abstract: DrugHarness is an evolvable agent harness that automates computational drug discovery by composing scientific operations and learning from feedback. It integrates diverse scientific resources and induces conditional skills, which are then verified by an independent agent. This allows DrugHarness to adapt its strategy for tasks like molecular screening and optimization, outperforming non-evolving systems.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of DrugHarness. (A) The agent composes public evidence, scientific tools, and code into task-specific workflows around shared scientific objects. Traces and permitted outcome feedback form experiences. (B) The learner induces conditional action hypotheses and translates them into candidate skills. An independent reviewer checks their evidence and conducts targeted trials in the same workspace when needed. Admitted skills guide subsequent tasks, while review records update insights and history for further learning.

top_papers.title: LocalIntent: Outcome-Specific Structured Generation for Backend-Compatible Smart Building Automation with Local LLMs
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces LocalIntent, a novel prompting strategy for local LLMs in smart building automation. It routes user requests to either command generation or persistent rule creation branches, followed by deterministic validation. LocalIntent significantly improves intent understanding and device identification compared to generic prompting methods, enabling backend-compatible smart building control with local LLMs.
top_papers.figure_caption: LocalIntent within a layered smart building automation platform.

top_papers.title: Advancing Clinical Genomic Analysis with a Skill-Centred Agent
top_papers.abstract: This paper introduces ClinGeX, a large-language-model agent designed to automate complex clinical genomic analysis. ClinGeX achieves this by orchestrating 105 executable skills, significantly outperforming existing methods in benchmark case classifications. Its core contribution is demonstrating a substantial improvement in the accuracy and efficiency of genomic analysis, facilitating faster clinical decision-making.
top_papers.figure_caption: Overview of ClinGeX and its evaluation. a. Task-oriented workflow. A clinical-genomics request and any accompanying text, image, PDF or other file types are submitted through the ClinGeX web application. The skill selector identifies the analytical needs, retrieves a task-specific subset of skills and their prerequisites, and passes them to the agent core for iterative planning, execution and evidence synthesis. b. Construction of the skill library. Candidate resources were identified through a broad domain scan, prioritised by LLM-assisted screening, reviewed by clinical and domain experts, and compiled and tested as 105 executable skills: 27 guide, 40 search and 38 analysis skills. Skills are connected by functional-relatedness and directed prerequisite edges. c. Controlled human-AI study. 45 readers evaluated 135 clinically derived cases across criterion-level variant analysis, genomic interpretation in rare disease and molecular oncology decision-making. d. Exploratory one-month deployment, where 11 clinical-genomics professionals submitted structured feedback on 96 completed analysis episodes.
